article_content: Even if you aren't a grown adult, you can still enjoy Japanese sumo wrestling, as demonstrated by these competitive kids. The National Children's Sumo Tournament in Tokyo featured boys of all shapes and sizes battling it out. The crowd went wild when Hayato Matsunaga, a smaller competitor, beat someone much bigger than him. One competitor showed his emotions openly after a match at the Tokyo tournament. Despite not being as big as some of their rivals, some wrestlers used skillful moves to win. These dedicated young athletes are among the many Japanese wrestlers participating in the yearly tournament, which is well-liked by sports fans all over the nation. Sumo is regarded as a modern martial art in Japan, despite having a history that goes back centuries. The annual event draws 300 young Japanese wrestlers and is very well-attended by sports enthusiasts nationwide. Sumo wrestling is a national obsession in Japan. The huge wrestlers, called rikishis, are viewed as national icons and unexpected sex symbols. Professional wrestlers may weigh more than 250 kg and must eat about 20,000 calories each day to stay in shape. In addition to their massive meals, the wrestlers drink about six pints of beer with each meal. During the bouts, the wrestlers focus intently on trying to force their opponents out of the ring. While they were very serious during their matches, the boys grinned as they observed the other competitors. Kaito Igarashi showed his disappointment after losing his fight in the competition. Even though sumo has been practiced for over a thousand years, the Japanese see it as a contemporary martial art. A dohyō, or circular ring, is the setting for the contests. The winner is the wrestler who first causes his opponent to either step outside of the ring or touch the ground with any body part other than their feet. Tradition is extremely important, and before each fight, the wrestlers do the Shiko ritual, stomping their feet to scare away evil spirits. The first boy to touch the ground with any part of his body except his soles loses, and these matches are typically brief, lasting under a minute. Parents proudly watched and cheered from the sidelines at Sunday's event.

article_content: By Emily Allen PUBLISHED: 11:49 EST, October 5, 2012 | UPDATED: 13:56 EST, October 5, 2012 Ahmad Otak today pleaded guilty to the double murder that occurred in March. An asylum-seeker today admitted to stabbing to death his ex-girlfriend's 17-year-old sister and her 18-year-old friend. Ahmad Otak, 21, murdered Kimberley Frank and her friend Samantha Sykes, 18, in Kimberley's flat in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, in March. Otak, who is from Afghanistan, had visited Kimberley's home to discuss his strained relationship with her sister Elisa when the murders took place. A judge at Leeds Crown Court today warned Otak that he now faces a life sentence. Appearing via video-link from Wakefield Prison, the 21-year-old - who entered the UK in 2007 - pleaded guilty to two counts of murder and to carrying a blade. Judge Peter Collier said in court: 'As I’m sure you will understand, the sentence for murder is fixed by law, and the sentence that will be passed on you in due course is one of life imprisonment.' Otak denied two further charges relating to the kidnap and false imprisonment of his ex-girlfriend, Elisa Frank. Richard Mansell, prosecuting, said the pleas were acceptable to the Crown and would be left on file. Otak also admitted to carrying a kitchen knife in Wakefield on the day of the murders. Steven Harratt, 57, of Wakefield, is accused of assisting an offender by giving Otak food, money, clothing, and a satellite navigation system after the murders. Otak stabbed Samantha Sykes, 18, to death at her friend's flat in Wakefield in March. Harratt denies the charge and was granted bail until his trial, the date of which is yet to be fixed. Otak was remanded in custody and will be sentenced on November 9. Otak's teenage victims were discovered at the flat in Barden Road in the Eastmoor area of Wakefield, West Yorkshire, on March 10. At the time, bunches of flowers were left on the steps leading up to the flats, and cards were attached to a handrail. A card on one of the bouquets read: 'Sammy, we will miss you sooo much. You were a great friend and will never ever be forgotten. We'll see you again one day. RIP.' West Yorkshire Police said that officers were contacted by Kent Police after a 19-year-old woman in Dover raised concerns for the safety of the two women. Officers went to the flat in Barden Road and discovered the bodies of Miss Frank and Miss Sykes, of California Drive, Horbury, West Yorkshire. A post-mortem examination revealed the women died from stab wounds. Miss Frank, who spent a large part of her life in care, had lived alone in the ground floor flat in the Eastmoor area of Wakefield since moving in two months earlier. Miss Sykes lived with her parents and younger brother, Ben, in a more affluent area of the town. Her parents, Eric and Julie, were too upset to speak. A police cordon was put in place, and officers stood guard at the flat in Wakefield after the teenage girls' bodies were discovered in March.

article_content: With Tamerlan Tsarnaev's widow agreeing to release his body, his uncle is now able to claim it; however, other family members could face arrest if they attempt to do so. Tamerlan Tsarnaev's body has remained at the Massachusetts medical examiner's office since his death in a gunfight with authorities over a week ago. Katherine Russell's attorney, Amato DeLuca from Rhode Island, stated that his client learned the medical examiner is ready to release Tsarnaev's body and she wishes for it to be released to his family. If Tsarnaev's mother travels to the U.S. to claim his remains, she risks potential arrest as the FBI considers Zubeidat Tsarnaeva a 'person of interest' in their investigation. Detectives are investigating whether she helped radicalize her son or had contact with other people or terrorist groups. Police noted that Tsarnaev ran out of ammunition before his brother, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, dragged his body under a vehicle while fleeing. The cause of death is determined but will remain private until the remains are claimed. Tsarnaev's uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, mentioned that family members will take possession of the body because 'a family is a family'. Tsarnaev's parents are in Russia, but he has other relatives in the U.S., including Tsarni. FBI agents visited Katherine Russell's parents' home in North Kingstown and removed several bags. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev is in a prison hospital recovering from injuries sustained in the shootout. He faces charges for using a weapon of mass destruction, which carries a possible death sentence. DeLuca stated Tamerlan Tsarnaev's widow has been cooperating with law enforcement and will continue to do so. Since taking refuge at her family's home on April 19, Russell has distanced herself from Tsarnaev, including reverting to her maiden name. DeLuca said Russell and her family are deeply saddened by the harm caused by the bombings. Terrel Harris from the Department of Public Safety noted that the state has not yet received Russell's request to release her husband's body. Harris mentioned that arrangements must be made before the body is released and a death certificate filed, and it is too early to speculate when that will occur.

Der Leichnam von Tamerlan Tsarnaev befindet sich seit seinem Tod bei einer Schießerei mit den Behörden vor über einer Woche im Leichenschauhaus von Massachusetts. Katherine Russells Anwalt, Amato DeLuca aus Rhode Island, erklärte, seine Mandantin habe erfahren, dass der Gerichtsmediziner bereit sei, Tsarnaevs Leichnam freizugeben, und dass sie wünscht, dass er an seine Familie übergeben wird. Sollte Tsarnaevs Mutter in die USA reisen, um seine sterblichen Überreste zu fordern, riskiert sie eine mögliche Verhaftung, da das FBI Zubeidat Tsarnaeva in ihren Ermittlungen als 'Person von Interesse' betrachtet. Die Ermittler prüfen, ob sie zur Radikalisierung ihres Sohnes beigetragen oder Kontakt zu anderen Personen oder terroristischen Vereinigungen hatte. Die Polizei stellte fest, dass Tsarnaev die Munition ausging, bevor sein Bruder, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, seinen Körper während der Flucht unter ein Fahrzeug zog. Die Todesursache ist zwar bekannt, wird aber erst nach der Freigabe des Leichnams veröffentlicht. Tsarnaevs Onkel, Ruslan Tsarni, erwähnte, dass Familienmitglieder den Leichnam in Besitz nehmen werden, da 'Familie Familie ist'. Tsarnaevs Eltern befinden sich in Russland, er hat jedoch weitere Verwandte in den USA, darunter Tsarni. FBI-Agenten suchten das Haus von Katherine Russells Eltern in North Kingstown auf und entfernten mehrere Säcke. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev befindet sich in einem Gefängniskrankenhaus und erholt sich von Verletzungen, die er bei der Schießerei erlitten hat. Ihm wird vorgeworfen, eine Massenvernichtungswaffe eingesetzt zu haben, was mit einer möglichen Todesstrafe geahndet wird. DeLuca erklärte, dass Tamerlan Tsarnaevs Witwe mit den Strafverfolgungsbehörden kooperiert hat und dies auch weiterhin tun wird. Seitdem sie am 19. April Zuflucht im Haus ihrer Familie suchte, hat sich Russell von Tsarnaev distanziert, unter anderem, indem sie wieder ihren Mädchennamen annahm. DeLuca sagte, Russell und ihre Familie seien zutiefst betrübt über das Leid, das durch die Bombenanschläge verursacht wurde. Terrel Harris von der Abteilung für öffentliche Sicherheit merkte an, dass der Staat noch keinen Antrag von Russell auf Freigabe des Leichnams ihres Mannes erhalten habe. Harris erwähnte, dass Vorkehrungen getroffen werden müssen, bevor der Leichnam freigegeben und eine Sterbeurkunde ausgestellt werden kann, und dass es zu früh sei, um zu spekulieren, wann dies geschehen wird.

article_content: During the family's visit to Australia and New Zealand, Prince George showcased his trendsetting style, mirroring his mother, the Duchess of Cambridge's, influence. Designers reported a significant sales surge due to the 'George effect', establishing the nine-month-old as a fashion icon. The young Royal debuted in New Zealand on April 7, demonstrating his ability to influence fashion trends. The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge arrived in New Zealand and Australia for their three-week Royal tour with Prince George. The Les Petites Abeilles romper suit worn in Sydney sold out rapidly, resulting in a two-month shipping delay. Prince George reacted in Prince William's arms after viewing an Australian Bilby named after him, wearing a blue outfit of shorts and t-shirt, again by Rachel Riley. Stockists of a novelty kangaroo backpack, carried by the Duke of Cambridge after being gifted to his son in Sydney, reported immediate sell-outs. The Australian Koala Foundation, a stockist of the bag, sold out its remaining stock instantly. Prince George departed Australia from Defense Establishment Fairbairn on April 25 in a red cardigan and striped red and white shorts, held by his mother, Kate. Prince George solidified his status as a style icon at the end of the Royal tour as the Duchess of Cambridge held him before boarding their flight in Canberra. CEO Deborah Tabart attributed the surge in orders for the kangaroo bag, priced at £7 (AUD$12.50), to Prince William carrying it. Even before the tour, Prince George's impact was evident. Following the family's Mother's Day portrait, where he wore a baby blue jumper with 'George' emblazoned on it, My1stYears.com sold 1200 jumpers in just four hours. Princess Diana was photographed with baby William in a similar outfit to George. Stockists confirmed the kangaroo bag sold out quickly after Prince William was seen with it. The 'Prince George effect' has boosted the high street as copycat clothes sell rapidly. The term originated when the £20 aden + anais cloth used to wrap Prince George leaving the Lindo Wing of St Mary's Hospital sold out quickly. According to style expert Nick Ede, a style icon creates trends, and Prince George does so with nautical stripes, dungarees, and baby grows with royal blue piping. Blue Almonds founder Izabela Minkiewicz noted Kate's major impact on fashion, predicting a similar effect on baby wear. Minkiewicz observed increased interest in Moses baskets and sales of similar infant beds after Kate was photographed in Blue Almonds while pregnant. Parents now request similar styles to George's outfits. Nick Ede added that Prince George's appeal lies in wearing wearable, affordable, and on-trend clothing suitable for the royal spotlight. He further stated that a style icon creates trends, which Prince George achieves with his choices. The 'George' printed jumper worn for the family's Mother's Day portrait was highly sought after. The Prince George effect began when the £20 printed white aden + anais cloth sold out quickly after the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge used it at the Lindo Wing of St Mary's Hospital.

article_content: Mohammed Khursheed Hussain, a 23-year-old IT student from India, has achieved a remarkable feat by setting a world record for typing with his nose. He secured the title by typing a sentence comprising 103 words on a keyboard. He accomplished this task in an impressive 47.44 seconds. The sentence read: 'Guinness World Records has challenged me to type this sentence using my nose in the fastest time.' This is not Mr. Hussain's first world record; he previously broke the record for typing the English alphabet with his fingers in just 3.43 seconds. Hussain mentioned that after his initial Guinness World Record in 2012, the support and motivation from his family and neighbors inspired him to pursue further achievements. He dedicated three years to practicing and improving his typing speed. Hussain revealed that he types with one eye closed to better locate the keys. article_content: Like a pop star saving their biggest hit for the encore, Sepp Blatter made sure to save his best for last. As a long day at the FIFA Congress in Sao Paulo came to an end, the 78-year-old announced he would stand for a fifth term, reneging on a promise he made four years prior. The news, which was expected, came after FIFA rejected proposals to impose age and term limits for officials. 'I know that my mandate will finish next year on May 29 in Zurich, but my mission is not finished,' he told Congress. 'And I tell you, together we will build the new FIFA. We have the foundations today because we have the budget for the next four years.' 'We have the foundation; now we work. Congress, you will decide who takes this great institution forward.' 'But I can tell you I am ready to accompany you in the future.' The Swiss official has been heavily criticized following corruption allegations related to FIFA's bidding process for the 2018 and 2022 World Cups. On Wednesday, several European members urged him not to run for president. Speaking after a tense meeting between Blatter and UEFA members, the mood within the European camp was unequivocally clear. David Gill, the English FA's representative on the Exco committee, said: 'The very fact that in 2011 he stated it was just for four years should have been the situation. To change his mind is disappointing.' 'I think we need a full, frank, and open debate about what FIFA needs going forward.' Only Jerome Champagne, a Frenchman, has declared he will oppose Blatter at the May 2015 Congress in Zurich, Switzerland. UEFA, the European governing body for soccer, has yet to reveal who it will select to contest the election. Michel Platini, the UEFA president, is not expected to challenge Blatter. Technology. As well as announcing his intention to continue in his role, Blatter also advocated for the increased use of technology within the game. The proposed idea would allow each manager two challenges to contest a refereeing decision, with television replays used to review the evidence. This World Cup will see goal-line technology used for the first time, but Blatter wants further changes. He told delegates: 'We could do something more on the field of play.' 'Why don't we give team managers the possibility of two challenges for refereeing decisions during the match? If the manager disagrees with a decision, why should he not ask for an immediate TV review with the referee?' The meeting also included a speech from U.S. lawyer Michael Garcia, appointed by FIFA to head an investigation into the bidding process for the 2018 and 2022 World Cups, awarded to Russia and Qatar respectively. Garcia has been tasked with probing bribery and corruption allegations, but his findings are not due to be made public until mid-July. His investigation has been brought into focus by a series of articles in the British newspaper The Sunday Times regarding the Qatar bid. The newspaper claims to have uncovered millions of emails and other documentation alleging that Qatar's former FIFA member, Mohamed Bin Hammam, used a multi-million dollar slush fund to buy support for the bid. Qatar organizers have strenuously denied the claims and, in a statement released to CNN Sunday, said they have been fully cooperating with Garcia's investigation. 'We remain totally confident that any objective inquiry will conclude we won the bid to host the 2022 FIFA World Cup fairly,' it added. These latest controversies come in the countdown to the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, which starts Thursday in Sao Paulo with a game between the hosts and Croatia.

article_content: Figures show police are using Taser stun guns on younger people daily. Officers deployed the 50,000-volt weapons against over 400 individuals under 18 in a single year, including some as young as 11. This marks a significant increase compared to seven years prior, when the devices were initially approved for use on this age group. Senior police officials are advocating for all 127,000 frontline officers nationwide to be equipped with Tasers. However, David Blunkett, the former Home Secretary who initially authorized the weapons in the UK, has voiced concerns that police are too quick to resort to Tasers instead of attempting to de-escalate tense situations. Records indicate that over 400 under-18s were Tasered by police, according to recent data. In an interview with BBC Radio 5 Live, he stated, 'I believe it is time for a review that includes guidance and support on utilizing Tasers and managing challenging situations effectively.' 'Using a Taser on an 11-year-old, in my opinion, is not the right approach, even in a difficult situation. We need to train officers to use more conventional methods.' Mr. Blunkett also urged chief constables to assess who is authorized to use Tasers and consider 'whether alternative methods can be employed.' According to the latest Home Office data, Tasers were used against 431 individuals under 18 in 2013, which is more than a third higher than the previous year. The data reveals that those Tasered included an 11-year-old, a 12-year-old, four 13-year-olds, and 33 14-year-olds. One Taser incident occurred at a Devon school for students with learning disabilities in December 2013. Police Tasered three students, aged 14 or 15, at Chelfham Senior School in Bere Alston after responding to a 'violent incident.' The 17-year-old age group was most frequently targeted, with around 180 incidents recorded, followed by 16-year-olds with 132 incidents. The statistics covered instances where Tasers were fired, used to 'light up' a target with a red dot, or simply removed from their holsters. Tasers were introduced in England and Wales in 2003 during a 12-month trial for firearms officers in five police forces. Four years later, police were authorized to use them on under-18s, resulting in 27 documented cases. In 2008, Tasers were implemented nationwide and were no longer restricted to specialized officers. Supporters argue that Tasers provide police with a crucial tool for resolving dangerous encounters without using lethal force. However, critics worry that Tasers are being used in routine situations to intimidate the public. There are also concerns about the improper use of Tasers, such as on individuals already in custody, those with mental health issues, and young or vulnerable people. Solicitor Sophie Khan, who represents individuals Tasered by police, stated, 'Tasers should only be used on children when there is no other viable way to restrain them.' But Met Commander Neil Basu said, 'If a 14-year-old is committing a violent act or is self-harming, our job is to stop that in the safest manner possible. In certain cases, a Taser is that option.'

Beamte setzten die 50.000-Volt-Waffen in einem einzigen Jahr gegen über 400 Minderjährige ein, darunter einige im Alter von nur 11 Jahren. Dies stellt einen deutlichen Anstieg gegenüber sieben Jahren zuvor dar, als die Geräte erstmals für den Einsatz in dieser Altersgruppe zugelassen wurden. Hochrangige Polizeibeamte setzen sich dafür ein, dass alle 127.000 Streifenpolizisten landesweit mit Tasern ausgestattet werden. David Blunkett, der ehemalige Innenminister, der die Waffen ursprünglich im Vereinigten Königreich genehmigt hat, äußerte jedoch Bedenken, dass die Polizei zu schnell auf Taser zurückgreift, anstatt zu versuchen, angespannte Situationen zu deeskalieren. Aufzeichnungen zeigen, dass laut aktuellen Daten über 400 Minderjährige von der Polizei getasert wurden. In einem Interview mit BBC Radio 5 Live erklärte er: 'Ich glaube, es ist Zeit für eine Überprüfung, die Leitlinien und Unterstützung für den Einsatz von Tasern und den effektiven Umgang mit schwierigen Situationen umfasst.' 'Meiner Meinung nach ist der Einsatz eines Tasers gegen einen 11-Jährigen selbst in einer schwierigen Situation nicht der richtige Ansatz. Wir müssen die Beamten darin schulen, konventionellere Methoden anzuwenden.' Herr Blunkett forderte die Polizeipräsidenten außerdem auf, zu prüfen, wer zum Einsatz von Tasern berechtigt ist, und zu überlegen, ob alternative Methoden eingesetzt werden können. Laut den neuesten Daten des Innenministeriums wurden Taser im Jahr 2013 gegen 431 Minderjährige eingesetzt, was einem Anstieg von mehr als einem Drittel gegenüber dem Vorjahr entspricht. Die Daten zeigen, dass zu den Getaserten ein 11-Jähriger, ein 12-Jähriger, vier 13-Jährige und 33 14-Jährige gehörten. Ein Taser-Vorfall ereignete sich im Dezember 2013 an einer Schule in Devon für Schüler mit Lernschwierigkeiten. Die Polizei hat drei Schüler im Alter von 14 oder 15 Jahren an der Chelfham Senior School in Bere Alston getasert, nachdem sie zu einem gewalttätigen Vorfall gerufen worden war. Die Altersgruppe der 17-Jährigen war mit rund 180 erfassten Vorfällen am häufigsten betroffen, gefolgt von den 16-Jährigen mit 132 Vorfällen. Die Statistiken umfassten Fälle, in denen Taser abgefeuert, zum 'Anleuchten' eines Ziels mit einem roten Punkt verwendet oder einfach aus dem Halfter genommen wurden. Taser wurden in England und Wales im Jahr 2003 im Rahmen eines 12-monatigen Versuchs für Schusswaffenbeamte in fünf Polizeikräften eingeführt. Vier Jahre später wurde die Polizei ermächtigt, sie gegen Minderjährige einzusetzen, was zu 27 dokumentierten Fällen führte. Im Jahr 2008 wurden Taser landesweit eingeführt und waren nicht mehr auf spezialisierte Beamte beschränkt. Befürworter argumentieren, dass Taser der Polizei ein wichtiges Instrument zur Verfügung stellen, um gefährliche Auseinandersetzungen ohne den Einsatz von tödlicher Gewalt zu lösen. Kritiker befürchten jedoch, dass Taser in routinemäßigen Situationen eingesetzt werden, um die Öffentlichkeit einzuschüchtern. Es gibt auch Bedenken hinsichtlich des unsachgemäßen Einsatzes von Tasern, beispielsweise gegen Personen, die sich bereits in Gewahrsam befinden, Personen mit psychischen Problemen sowie junge oder schutzbedürftige Personen. Die Anwältin Sophie Khan, die von der Polizei getaserte Personen vertritt, erklärte: 'Taser sollten bei Kindern nur dann eingesetzt werden, wenn es keine andere praktikable Möglichkeit gibt, sie zu bändigen.' Aber Met Commander Neil Basu sagte: 'Wenn ein 14-Jähriger eine Gewalttat begeht oder sich selbst verletzt, ist es unsere Aufgabe, dies auf die sicherste Art und Weise zu verhindern. In bestimmten Fällen ist ein Taser diese Option.'

article_content: Manchester City has no intention of selling striker Alvaro Negredo. Sources indicate the Spaniard is not for sale, despite increased speculation linking him with Atletico Madrid. The club has not received any formal bid from, nor had any contact with, the Spanish champions regarding a potential £20 million move, as reported. The club would not welcome such offers and values the 28-year-old higher than the reported £20 million, which is what they paid Sevilla last summer. Negredo made a significant impact at the Etihad Stadium last season, scoring 23 goals in all competitions. However, his last goal was in January, after which he experienced a decline in form due to a shoulder injury. This slump resulted in him missing a place in the Spain squad for the World Cup in Brazil. Reports suggest he is unsettled and is being considered as a potential replacement for Diego Costa at Atletico, who is likely to join Chelsea. Negredo is from Madrid and began his career with Real Madrid. However, City intends to retain him as part of their striking options, which include Sergio Aguero, Edin Dzeko, and Stevan Jovetic. Atletico Madrid is reportedly interested in Negredo, but City values him at more than £20 million. City manager Manuel Pellegrini wishes to keep the Spanish striker at the Etihad next season.

article_content: Bryan Singer, the director of 'Superman Returns,' is again facing accusations. A man, now 25, filed a lawsuit alleging Singer sexually assaulted him when he was a minor. The lawsuit claims that Singer, along with Broadway producer Gary Goddard, coerced the man into sexual acts, promising to help his acting career. Similar charges have been made by Michael Egan against Singer and other executives, who have also denied any wrongdoing. Egan's attorney urged other victims to come forward. article_content: A high-ranking mafia member, Francesco Palmeri, has been arrested in New York City. Palmeri, associated with the Gambino crime family, was apprehended after allegedly attempting to extort $1.23 million from an Italian businessman. Following his arrest, he was extradited to Italy to face court proceedings. Palmeri traveled to Italy twice in 2013, reportedly to pressure the owner of a southern Italian company specializing in electrical systems for oil platforms. The businessman also received threatening letters, purportedly from 'friends in Brooklyn,' demanding money, as stated in the warrant. The warrant indicates the extortion involved a loan from the 1980s, suspected to originate from international drug traffickers linked to the late New York mobster Cesare Bonventre, who shared a birthplace, Castellammare del Golfo, Sicily, with Palmeri. The extortion case surfaced during a separate investigation into a trans-Atlantic drug smuggling and money laundering operation involving members of the Calabrian 'Ndrangheta and the Gambino family. If convicted, Palmeri faces a potential prison sentence of up to 20 years. Andrea Grassi, an investigator with the Italian anti-mafia police unit SCO, stated, 'This demonstrates the international reach of the 'Ndrangheta and Cosa Nostra and their enduring ties with the historic New York mob families.' Investigators noted that the maximum sentence for criminal conspiracy to commit international extortion, aggravated by mafia membership, is approximately 20 years.

article_content: Barcelona and the Catalonia region are at a crossroads regarding bullfighting, a long-standing Spanish custom. The regional parliament is scheduled to vote this Wednesday on a potential ban. If the ban is approved, Catalonia would distinguish itself as the first region in mainland Spain to prohibit bullfighting. Some observers perceive this as a rebuke to the rest of the nation. Enrique Guillen, a 24-year-old bullfighter, expresses concern that he may be the last Barcelona native to take the 'alternativa'. This is a ceremonial bullfight against large bulls to become a fully qualified matador, a feat he accomplished last year at Barcelona's only remaining bullring, the Monumental. Guillen's father worked at the Monumental, facilitating the entry of bulls into the arena. 'My father introduced me to bullfights when I was very young,' Guillen recalls. 'It would be disappointing not to share with my children what my parents shared with me.' Conversely, Aida Gascon, an activist with the Anti-Bullfighting Party (PACMA), focuses on animal welfare, deeming bullfighting cruel. She recounts attending only one bullfight to witness the bull's suffering, which she captured in a painting displayed in her home. 'Bullfighting is ingrained in Spanish culture,' Gascon acknowledges. 'However, culture evolves. Many traditions fade as society progresses.' Across Spain, the frequency of bullfights has decreased by approximately one-third in recent years, primarily due to budgetary limitations affecting local governments that often subsidize these events. In Catalonia, only a little over a dozen bullfights occur annually, with the Monumental bullring in Barcelona serving as virtually the sole venue. Luis Corrales and his pro-bullfight organization, PPDF, have issued a study forecasting substantial economic repercussions for Catalonia if bullfighting is outlawed. These losses, according to Corrales, would mainly arise from the Catalan government's obligation to compensate the bullfighting industry, which possesses long-term operating licenses. Corrales questions how the Catalan government can justify large indemnity payments when they are trying to cut the budget. Critics contend that the economic consequences would be insignificant, considering the limited number of bullfights currently held in Catalonia. Regardless, the Catalan parliament's vote on bullfighting is attracting attention both within Spain and internationally. The proposal to ban bullfighting originated as a grassroots initiative in Catalonia and received parliamentary consideration last year by a narrow vote. Since then, the debate has intensified, with proponents and opponents gathering support from across Spain and even abroad. Most analysts predict a close vote on Wednesday. The two largest parties in parliament, the ruling Socialists and the opposition Catalan nationalists (CiU), have allowed their members to vote according to their conscience. Smaller left-leaning parties are likely to support the ban, while the conservative Popular Party is expected to advocate for maintaining the tradition. If approved, the ban would take effect in January 2012 and would not extend to the rest of Spain. Bullfighting remains popular in Madrid and Seville. While the Canary Islands already prohibit bullfighting, a ban in Catalonia would represent a more substantial setback for the tradition. Some commentators suggest that Catalan nationalism, including separatist sentiments, and the upcoming regional elections, are influencing the vote. However, the primary advocates on both sides assert that the core issue is the conflict between tradition and animal protection. The Catalan parliament vote is expected by 1 p.m. (7 a.m. ET) Wednesday.
translated_content: Barcelona und die Region Katalonien stehen an einem Scheideweg bezüglich des Stierkampfs, einem langjährigen spanischen Brauch. Das Regionalparlament soll an diesem Mittwoch über ein mögliches Verbot abstimmen. Wenn das Verbot angenommen wird, würde sich Katalonien als die erste Region auf dem spanischen Festland auszeichnen, die den Stierkampf verbietet. Einige Beobachter sehen dies als eine Zurechtweisung des restlichen Landes. Enrique Guillen, ein 24-jähriger Stierkämpfer, äußert die Sorge, dass er der letzte in Barcelona geborene Stierkämpfer sein könnte, der die 'Alternativa' antritt. Dies ist ein zeremonieller Stierkampf gegen große Stiere, um ein vollwertiger Matador zu werden, eine Leistung, die er letztes Jahr in Barcelonas einzig verbliebener Stierkampfarena, dem Monumental, vollbrachte. Guillens Vater arbeitete im Monumental und erleichterte den Einlass der Stiere in die Arena. 'Mein Vater hat mich schon in jungen Jahren mit zu Stierkämpfen genommen', erinnert sich Guillen. 'Es wäre enttäuschend, meinen Kindern nicht das weitergeben zu können, was meine Eltern mir gegeben haben.' Im Gegensatz dazu konzentriert sich Aida Gascon, eine Aktivistin der Anti-Stierkampf-Partei (PACMA), auf das Tierwohl und betrachtet den Stierkampf als grausam. Sie erzählt, dass sie nur einen Stierkampf besucht hat, um das Leiden des Stieres mitzuerleben, das sie in einem Gemälde festhielt, das in ihrem Haus ausgestellt ist. 'Der Stierkampf ist in der spanischen Kultur verwurzelt', räumt Gascon ein. 'Die Kultur entwickelt sich jedoch weiter. Viele Traditionen verschwinden mit dem Fortschritt der Gesellschaft.' In ganz Spanien hat die Häufigkeit von Stierkämpfen in den letzten Jahren um etwa ein Drittel abgenommen, vor allem aufgrund von Haushaltsbeschränkungen, die sich auf die lokalen Regierungen auswirken, die diese Veranstaltungen oft subventionieren. In Katalonien finden jährlich nur etwas mehr als ein Dutzend Stierkämpfe statt, wobei die Stierkampfarena Monumental in Barcelona praktisch der einzige Austragungsort ist. Luis Corrales und seine Pro-Stierkampf-Organisation PPDF haben eine Studie veröffentlicht, die erhebliche wirtschaftliche Auswirkungen für Katalonien vorhersagt, falls der Stierkampf verboten wird. Diese Verluste würden laut Corrales hauptsächlich aus der Verpflichtung der katalanischen Regierung resultieren, die Stierkampf-Industrie zu entschädigen, die über langfristige Betriebsgenehmigungen verfügt. Corrales fragt, wie die katalanische Regierung große Entschädigungszahlungen rechtfertigen kann, wenn sie versucht, den Haushalt zu kürzen. Kritiker argumentieren, dass die wirtschaftlichen Folgen unbedeutend wären, angesichts der geringen Anzahl von Stierkämpfen, die derzeit in Katalonien stattfinden. Ungeachtet dessen zieht die Abstimmung des katalanischen Parlaments über den Stierkampf sowohl innerhalb Spaniens als auch international Aufmerksamkeit auf sich. Der Vorschlag, den Stierkampf zu verbieten, entstand als Graswurzelinitiative in Katalonien und wurde im vergangenen Jahr mit knapper Mehrheit vom Parlament zur Prüfung angenommen. Seitdem hat sich die Debatte intensiviert, wobei Befürworter und Gegner Unterstützung aus ganz Spanien und sogar aus dem Ausland sammeln. Die meisten Analysten prognostizieren ein knappes Ergebnis am Mittwoch. Die beiden größten Parteien im Parlament, die regierenden Sozialisten und die oppositionellen katalanischen Nationalisten (CiU), haben ihren Mitgliedern erlaubt, nach ihrem Gewissen abzustimmen. Kleinere linke Parteien werden das Verbot wahrscheinlich unterstützen, während die konservative Volkspartei voraussichtlich für die Aufrechterhaltung der Tradition eintreten wird. Wenn es angenommen wird, würde das Verbot im Januar 2012 in Kraft treten und sich nicht auf den Rest Spaniens erstrecken. Der Stierkampf ist in Madrid und Sevilla nach wie vor populär. Während die Kanarischen Inseln den Stierkampf bereits verbieten, wäre ein Verbot in Katalonien ein erheblicherer Rückschlag für die Tradition. Einige Kommentatoren vermuten, dass der katalanische Nationalismus, einschließlich separatistischer Bestrebungen, und die bevorstehenden Regionalwahlen die Abstimmung beeinflussen. Die Hauptvertreter beider Seiten betonen jedoch, dass der Kern der Auseinandersetzung der Konflikt zwischen Tradition und Tierschutz ist. Die Abstimmung des katalanischen Parlaments wird für 13.00 Uhr (7.00 Uhr ET) am Mittwoch erwartet.

article_content: A couple survived a fall of over 400ft from Helvellyn, England's third highest mountain, thanks to a rescue team training nearby. The married pair, believed to be from Herefordshire, were hiking the 3,117ft Swirral Edge on Helvellyn – known as one of the more challenging routes in the Lake District. Reports indicate the husband slipped and fell first at around 3:30 pm on Sunday, plummeting approximately 420ft into Brown Cove. His wife then fell while attempting to prevent his fall. She is thought to have fallen even further, tumbling down the rocky mountainside and stopping about 500ft below. Another walker witnessed the incident and contacted emergency services. Fortunately, a Patterdale mountain rescue team was training nearby and arrived on scene within minutes. The 13-member team, later assisted by members of Calder Valley MRT, RAF mountain rescue, and Kendal MRT, worked to rescue the couple as darkness descended. An RAF Sea King helicopter from Boulmer, Northumberland, airlifted them to Cumberland Infirmary. Remarkably, neither sustained life-threatening injuries; the wife suffered cuts and bruises, and the husband sustained minor neck injuries. Mike Blakey, Team Leader of Patterdale Mountain Rescue, stated: 'The ridge is notorious for accidents, and the couple are extremely fortunate to have survived, especially considering they both fell.' 'It was also fortunate that we were nearby to assist, having just completed a training session.' 'As a team, we emphasize that the mountain is currently in full winter conditions.' 'It is very icy up there, and ice axes are necessary to navigate the fells.' 'People must ensure they are properly equipped before venturing out.' He added that he couldn't confirm weather as a factor but noted that conditions on the high fells are wintry this time of year. He urged those adventuring in the Lakes to bring winter walking equipment, including ice axes, crampons, and a torch. Helvellyn is the third-highest mountain in England, according to Hills in England, Wales and Ireland over Two Thousand Feet (Hewitts). Scafell Pike and Scafell are the first and second highest at 3,200ft and 3,162ft, respectively. Ben Nevis is the highest in the British Isles at 4,409ft.
translated_content: Ein Ehepaar überlebte einen Sturz von über 120 Metern vom Helvellyn, dem dritthöchsten Berg Englands, dank eines Rettungsteams, das in der Nähe trainierte. Das verheiratete Paar, vermutlich aus Herefordshire, wanderte auf dem 950 Meter hohen Swirral Edge am Helvellyn – bekannt als eine der anspruchsvollsten Routen im Lake District. Berichten zufolge rutschte der Ehemann zuerst aus und stürzte gegen 15:30 Uhr am Sonntag etwa 128 Meter tief in die Brown Cove. Seine Frau stürzte dann, als sie versuchte, seinen Fall zu verhindern. Es wird vermutet, dass sie noch weiter fiel, den felsigen Berghang hinunter und etwa 150 Meter tiefer zum Stillstand kam. Ein anderer Wanderer wurde Zeuge des Vorfalls und alarmierte die Rettungsdienste. Glücklicherweise trainierte ein Bergrettungsteam von Patterdale in der Nähe und traf innerhalb weniger Minuten am Unfallort ein. Das 13-köpfige Team, das später von Mitgliedern des Calder Valley MRT, der RAF-Bergrettung und des Kendal MRT unterstützt wurde, arbeitete daran, das Paar zu retten, als die Dunkelheit hereinbrach. Ein RAF Sea King-Hubschrauber aus Boulmer, Northumberland, flog sie in das Cumberland Infirmary. Bemerkenswerterweise erlitt keiner von beiden lebensbedrohliche Verletzungen; die Frau erlitt Schnittwunden und Prellungen, und der Ehemann erlitt leichte Nackenverletzungen. Mike Blakey, Teamleiter der Patterdale Mountain Rescue, sagte: 'Der Grat ist berüchtigt für Unfälle, und das Paar hat großes Glück, überlebt zu haben, besonders wenn man bedenkt, dass beide gestürzt sind.' 'Es war auch ein Glück, dass wir in der Nähe waren, um zu helfen, nachdem wir gerade eine Trainingseinheit beendet hatten.' 'Als Team betonen wir, dass auf dem Berg derzeit winterliche Bedingungen herrschen.' 'Es ist sehr eisig dort oben, und Eisäxte sind notwendig, um sich auf den Felsen zu bewegen.' 'Man muss sicherstellen, dass man richtig ausgerüstet ist, bevor man sich auf den Weg macht.' Er fügte hinzu, dass er das Wetter nicht als Ursache bestätigen könne, aber die Bedingungen auf den hohen Bergen seien zu dieser Jahreszeit winterlich. Er forderte Wanderer im Lake District auf, Winterausrüstung wie Eisäxte, Steigeisen und eine Taschenlampe mitzubringen. Der Helvellyn ist laut Hills in England, Wales und Irland über Two Thousand Feet (Hewitts) der dritthöchste Berg Englands. Scafell Pike und Scafell sind mit 975 Metern bzw. 964 Metern die höchsten beiden Berge. Der Ben Nevis ist mit 1344 Metern der höchste Berg Großbritanniens.

article_content: Families are facing the possibility of canceled holidays due to significant delays at the Passport Office, which is struggling with a large backlog of applications. The overwhelmed Passport Office is struggling to issue travel documents in a timely manner, potentially preventing families from going on holiday. As many as 500,000 individuals may not receive their passports before their planned departure dates as the understaffed department struggles with the annual surge in applications. Both Labour and Conservative MPs have expressed concerns about the service's disarray, reporting numerous complaints from constituents regarding delays. While passport changes and new passport issuances typically take three to four weeks, travelers report processing times are now twice as long. Some travelers have been advised to pay an additional £55.50 to expedite their passports, supposedly guaranteeing on-time arrival. In an effort to address the crisis, 25% of the staff responsible for detecting fraudulent paperwork have been reassigned to process the thousands of delayed applications. David Hanson, Labour’s immigration spokesman, has cautioned that reducing the fraud detection teams poses a ‘real worry’ to the integrity and security of the passport system. Mr. Hanson stated that Labour MPs have received over 400 complaints in the last six weeks from constituents struggling to obtain passports in time for their holidays and international trips. Since January, the Passport Office, a division of the Home Office, has received approximately 300,000 more applications than during the same period last year, attributing the increase to ‘the improving economy and a rise in holiday bookings’. Unions, however, have argued that job cuts and office closures have rendered the Passport Office unable to manage the current demand as the summer holidays approach. Approximately 80 staff members, including about a quarter of the fraud team, are being redeployed in a ‘last push’ to resolve the backlog, according to a leaked email from Paul Pugh, head of the Passport Office. Mr. Pugh acknowledged ‘work-in-progress levels which are much higher than we would like’ and noted ‘We have seen very high volumes of contact with Members of Parliament.’ Mr. Hanson intends to discuss the reassignment of anti-fraud staff with the Home Secretary, expressing ‘serious concerns’ that Theresa May’s ‘mismanagement of resources’ has left the passport service understaffed in its anti-fraud measures. He stated, ‘This is absolutely unacceptable and is a real worry to the integrity and security of the passport system.’ Richard Harrington, Conservative MP for Watford, has also submitted a parliamentary question regarding the delays after receiving six complaints in one week. In a statement, Mr. Pugh said that additional staff had been hired to meet the increased demand and that the office was operating seven days a week. He added, ‘We have processed more than 97% of straightforward passport renewal and child applications within the three-week target turnaround time. There is no backlog, with over 99% of straightforward applications being processed within four weeks.’ The Home Office clarified that the fraud team staff who had been reassigned were working on long-term investigations rather than checking applications. In the summer of 1999, at least 500 holidaymakers missed their departure dates due to problems at the then Passport Agency when a new computer system prevented it from issuing passports on time.

article_content: To commemorate Russia's 'reunification' with Crimea, a Russian foundry recently created a new coin. It features Vladimir Putin's image on one side and a map of Crimea on the other. The term 'reunification' is often contested, particularly outside of Russia. The coin's symbolism extends far beyond simple Russian pride concerning the small Black Sea peninsula. Many Russians, especially those who recall the Soviet era and the presidency of Boris Yeltsin, associate Putin's influence with their financial well-being. When Putin assumed the presidency at the close of the last millennium, Russia was still recovering from the 1998 economic downturn. The IMF's October 1999 World Economic Outlook noted ongoing economic and political uncertainties, leading to capital flight and reduced foreign investment. Putin then addressed these issues by reducing income and corporate taxes and streamlining bureaucracy. Boosted by rising oil prices, Russia's economy grew rapidly, averaging 7% over the following eight years. Russians had more money and increased opportunities. Prosperity and stability became highly valued, even at the expense of democracy. Fourteen years later, the IMF's latest World Economic Outlook highlighted unsettling similarities to 1999. Russia's growth prospects were lowered due to 'geopolitical risks'. The IMF observed that investment was already weak, partly due to policy uncertainty. Standard and Poor's mirrored this assessment by downgrading Russia's credit rating to just above junk status. It would be overly optimistic to call this a simple return to the starting point. In 1999, Russia was already emerging from a decline when Putin took office. Now, it may be heading downward. While Russia's economy benefits from about $477 billion in foreign currency reserves, sanctions could still have a severe impact, and there's the crucial factor of perception. According to Andrei Konoplyanik, an advisor to Gazprom Export, ratings downgrades and lowered forecasts are causing immediate anxiety within the investment community. Russia may not need external validation, but it does require foreign capital. In a 2008 speech outlining Russia's objectives up to 2020, Putin stated that Russia doesn't seek to take anything from anyone, emphasizing the country's self-sufficiency and lack of desire for isolation. But, is Putin ready to sacrifice Russia's remaining economic stability in this pursuit?

Viele Russen, besonders diejenigen, die sich an die Sowjetära und die Präsidentschaft von Boris Jelzin erinnern, verbinden Putins Einfluss mit ihrem finanziellen Wohlergehen. Als Putin zum Ende des letzten Jahrtausends die Präsidentschaft übernahm, erholte sich Russland noch vom Wirtschaftsabschwung 1998. Der World Economic Outlook des IWF vom Oktober 1999 wies auf anhaltende wirtschaftliche und politische Unsicherheiten hin, was zu Kapitalflucht und geringeren ausländischen Investitionen führte. Putin ging diese Probleme dann an, indem er die Einkommen- und Körperschaftssteuer senkte und die Bürokratie straffte. Angetrieben durch steigende Ölpreise wuchs die russische Wirtschaft rasant und erreichte in den folgenden acht Jahren durchschnittlich 7%. Die Russen hatten mehr Geld und mehr Möglichkeiten. Wohlstand und Stabilität wurden hoch geschätzt, selbst auf Kosten der Demokratie. Vierzehn Jahre später hob der jüngste World Economic Outlook des IWF beunruhigende Ähnlichkeiten zu 1999 hervor. Russlands Wachstumsaussichten wurden aufgrund von 'geopolitischen Risiken' gesenkt. Der IWF stellte fest, dass Investitionen bereits schwach waren, was teilweise auf politische Unsicherheit zurückzuführen war. Standard & Poor's spiegelte diese Einschätzung wider, indem sie Russlands Kreditwürdigkeit auf knapp über Ramschniveau herabstufte. Es wäre übertrieben optimistisch, dies als einfache Rückkehr zum Ausgangspunkt zu bezeichnen. 1999 erholte sich Russland bereits von einem Abschwung, als Putin das Amt übernahm. Jetzt könnte es wieder abwärts gehen. Während die russische Wirtschaft von etwa 477 Milliarden Dollar an Devisenreserven profitiert, könnten Sanktionen dennoch schwerwiegende Auswirkungen haben, und es gibt den entscheidenden Faktor der Wahrnehmung. Russland braucht vielleicht keine externe Bestätigung, aber es braucht ausländisches Kapital. In einer Rede aus dem Jahr 2008, in der Putin die Ziele Russlands bis 2020 umriss, erklärte er, dass Russland nicht versucht, irgendjemandem etwas wegzunehmen, und betonte die Autarkie des Landes und den fehlenden Wunsch nach Isolation. Aber ist Putin bereit, die verbleibende wirtschaftliche Stabilität Russlands für dieses Ziel zu opfern?

article_content: According to historical trends, skirt lengths might indicate economic health. The prevalence of longer skirts on the high street suggests a potentially struggling economy. Hemlines are at their longest since the Great Depression, with celebrities like Victoria Beckham sporting below-the-knee styles. However, the Hemline Index indicates a possible upturn. This index, developed by economist George Taylor, links shorter skirts to economic prosperity. While Victoria Beckham has been seen in long skirts, the index suggests brighter economic times may be ahead. Historically, longer skirts have signaled economic decline, particularly during recessions. The last time maxi skirts were fashionable was in the early nineties when inflation reached 15 percent. Conversely, the 1960s, with the rise of the mini skirt, and the late 1990s, marked by economic boom and 18-inch skirts, reflected financial highs. Despite shop windows displaying maxi-length pencil skirts, suggesting a bleak economic outlook, the Hemline Index offers a more optimistic view. While last year's Autumn/Winter runways featured longer hemlines, recent observations suggest the economy may improve by the time these trends become mainstream fashion. Prime Minister David Cameron cautioned that economic difficulties may persist until the decade's end. Economic experts and the Bank of England share this cautious outlook, with the Bank recently reducing Britain's predicted growth for 2012 to zero. Governor Sir Mervyn King cited eurozone developments and rising energy prices as factors impacting growth. Economists described a recent inflation report as notably disheartening, forecasting economic growth to peak at just 2.25 percent in 2014 and 2015. This represents the lowest peak forecast since the Bank of England gained independence in 1997.

Historisch gesehen haben längere Röcke einen wirtschaftlichen Abschwung signalisiert, insbesondere während Rezessionen. Das letzte Mal, dass Maxiröcke in Mode waren, war in den frühen neunziger Jahren, als die Inflation 15 Prozent erreichte. Umgekehrt spiegelten die 1960er Jahre mit dem Aufkommen des Minirocks und die späten 1990er Jahre, die von einem Wirtschaftsboom und 18-Zoll-Röcken geprägt waren, wirtschaftliche Höhen wider. Während die Herbst/Winter-Laufstege des letzten Jahres längere Säume zeigten, deuten aktuelle Beobachtungen darauf hin, dass sich die Wirtschaft möglicherweise verbessert, bis diese Trends zum Mainstream werden. Dies ist die niedrigste Höchststandsprognose seit der Unabhängigkeit der Bank of England im Jahr 1997.

article_content: South Australian Senator Penny Wong shared that keeping her family's joyful secret proved difficult after telling her three-year-old daughter, Alexandra, that she would soon have a sibling. Senator Wong, a member of the Labor Party, and her partner, Sophie Allouache, announced they are expecting their second child in April, much to the delight of their eldest child. Senator Wong told 'The Advertiser' in Adelaide, 'Like many families, we considered whether to tell our toddler, knowing her penchant for sharing information. Ultimately, we decided it was important for her to be aware.' The excited Alexandra apparently couldn't contain the news. Senator Wong recounted, 'At the Labor convention, she repeatedly read 'The Gruffalo' to a baby. When I checked in, a friend mentioned that all was well, except Alexandra had informed everyone that Mummy has a baby in her tummy.' Reports indicate that the couple conceived both children through IVF, utilizing the same sperm donor. Senator Wong acknowledged the invaluable support from her mother and Sophie Allouache's family in raising their family. She admitted that balancing motherhood with her demanding political career presents considerable challenges. 'I believe our society still has significant progress to make regarding work-family balance,' she stated. This issue of work-family balance is anticipated to return to the forefront of political discussion, as the Abbott government plans to review childcare funding and its debated paid parental leave scheme early next year. Senator Wong is among three Labor politicians anticipating new additions to their families in 2015, with Labor frontbenchers Kate Ellis and Amanda Rishworth also expecting babies in the New Year.

article_content: Mick Jagger recently celebrated his 70th birthday. It's remarkable that such a major figure in music remains active and stylish even as he enters what many consider retirement age. Here are some interesting facts about the iconic artist's colorful life and impressive career: He had two marriages: first to Bianca Jagger from 1971 to 1979, and later to Jerry Hall from 1990 to 1999. Jagger has seven children: Karis (born in 1970), Jade (1971), Elizabeth (1984), James (1985), Georgia (1992), Gabriel (1997), and Lucas (1999). The Rolling Stones have released 29 studio albums and achieved eight No. 1 singles on Billboard's Hot 100 chart. They also boast 36 Top 10 albums on the Billboard 200. As a solo artist, Jagger has released five albums, with 'She's the Boss' (1985) achieving platinum status in the United States. The Rolling Stones' greatest hits album 'Hot Rocks' has reached platinum status 12 times, selling over 12 million copies in the United States. He has won two Grammy Awards: one for the Rolling Stones' album 'Voodoo Lounge' (1994) and another for the group's song 'Love Is Strong' (1994). The band also received a Lifetime Achievement Award in 1996. Jagger has received 15 Grammy nominations for both his solo work and collaborations with the Rolling Stones. A lock of Jagger's hair was sold for approximately $6,000 (£4,000) at a Bonhams auction in London in July. Jagger met his future bandmate, Keith Richards, at the young age of 5. A species of trilobite, Aegrotocatellus Jaggeri, was named in his honor. This ancient arthropod lived in what is now Nunavut, Canada, around 542 million years ago.

article_content: North Korea on Thursday defended its right to explore outer space following reports that a rocket, which the United States believes to be a long-range missile, had been positioned on its launch pad. Replicas of South and North Korean missiles are displayed at the Korea War Memorial in Seoul. North Korea recently informed two U.N. agencies of its plans to launch a satellite. The launch is expected to occur between April 4 and April 8, according to Yonhap, South Korea's news agency. North Korea's announcement has triggered international concern. Officials from the U.S. and South Korea have stated that North Korea is likely preparing to test a long-range missile, disguised as a satellite launch. Pyongyang responded to critics on Thursday with a commentary published by the state-run KCNA news service. 'This is nothing but a groundless outcry from political philistines who are ignorant of the legality of space science research for peaceful purposes,' the commentary stated. 'Outer space is not a monopoly of a few specified powers but an asset common to mankind, and space development is being promoted worldwide.' Should all nations have the right to explore space? U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton said Wednesday in an interview with CNN's Jill Dougherty that the United States does not plan to shoot down the North Korean rocket, but will raise the issue with the U.N. Security Council if Pyongyang proceeds with the launch. 'We are doing our best to dissuade the North Koreans from going forward, because it is a provocative action,' Clinton said. 'It raises questions about their compliance with Security Council Resolution 1718. And if they persist, we will address it through appropriate channels.' According to Kim Taewoo, an expert at the Korea Institute for Defense Analyses, North Korea is technically capable of launching a rocket in as little as two to four days. However, he doubts that a launch will occur so soon. Kim said that it would not be logical for Pyongyang to make such a move after formally announcing its plans. 'North Korea could delay the launch if they encounter problems with the weather or internal issues, but I don't see any reason why they would launch it ahead of schedule,' Kim said. U.S. officials have stated that the purpose of the North Korean launch may not be known until it occurs. A U.N. Security Council resolution in 2006 prohibited North Korea from conducting ballistic missile activity. Japanese officials stated that they could shoot down the object, regardless of whether it is a missile or a satellite. 'As U.N. resolutions prohibit North Korea from engaging in ballistic missile activities, we still consider it to be a violation from a technical standpoint, even if North Korea claims it is a satellite. We will discuss the matter with related countries based on this view,' Japanese Foreign Minister Hirofumi Nakasone said earlier this month. South Korea echoed Clinton's statements. 'The South Korean government believes that if North Korea proceeds with the launch despite continuous warnings from the South Korean government and the international community, it will be a provocative action that constitutes a serious threat to the security of northeast Asia and the Korean peninsula,' said Foreign Ministry spokesman Moon Tae-Young. 'The launch of the long-range rocket is a clear violation of U.N. Security Council Resolution No. 1718, and we strongly urge North Korea to immediately cease such measures.' The North Korean Taepodong-2 missile is believed to have a range of approximately 6,700 kilometers (4,200 miles), which, if accurate, would allow it to strike Alaska or Hawaii. CNN's Pam Benson contributed to this report.
translated_content: Nordkorea verteidigte am Donnerstag sein Recht, den Weltraum zu erkunden, nachdem Berichte aufkamen, wonach eine Rakete, von der die Vereinigten Staaten annehmen, dass es sich um eine Langstreckenrakete handelt, auf ihrer Startrampe positioniert wurde. Nachbildungen südkoreanischer und nordkoreanischer Raketen sind im Korea-Kriegsdenkmal in Seoul ausgestellt. Nordkorea informierte kürzlich zwei UN-Organisationen über seine Pläne, einen Satelliten zu starten. Der Start wird voraussichtlich zwischen dem 4. und 8. April stattfinden, laut Yonhap, der südkoreanischen Nachrichtenagentur. Die Ankündigung Nordkoreas hat internationale Besorgnis ausgelöst. Beamte der USA und Südkoreas haben erklärt, dass Nordkorea wahrscheinlich einen Langstreckenraketentest vorbereitet, der als Satellitenstart getarnt ist. Pjöngjang reagierte am Donnerstag auf Kritik mit einem Kommentar, der vom staatlichen Nachrichtendienst KCNA veröffentlicht wurde. 'Dies ist nichts als ein unbegründeter Aufschrei politischer Philister, die die Rechtmäßigkeit der Weltraumforschung für friedliche Zwecke ignorieren', hieß es in dem Kommentar. 'Der Weltraum ist kein Monopol einiger weniger Mächte, sondern ein gemeinsames Gut der Menschheit, und die Weltraumentwicklung wird weltweit gefördert.' Sollten alle Nationen das Recht haben, den Weltraum zu erforschen? US-Außenministerin Hillary Clinton sagte am Mittwoch in einem Interview mit Jill Dougherty von CNN, dass die Vereinigten Staaten nicht planen, die nordkoreanische Rakete abzuschießen, aber das Problem mit dem UN-Sicherheitsrat erörtern werden, sollte Pjöngjang den Start durchführen. 'Wir tun unser Bestes, um die Nordkoreaner davon abzubringen, weiterzumachen, weil es eine provokative Handlung ist', sagte Clinton. 'Es wirft Fragen hinsichtlich ihrer Einhaltung der Resolution 1718 des Sicherheitsrates auf. Und wenn sie darauf bestehen, werden wir uns über geeignete Kanäle damit befassen.' Laut Kim Taewoo, einem Experten des Korea-Instituts für Verteidigungsanalysen, ist Nordkorea technisch in der Lage, eine Rakete in nur zwei bis vier Tagen zu starten. Er bezweifelt jedoch, dass ein Start so bald erfolgen wird. Kim sagte, es wäre nicht logisch für Pjöngjang, einen solchen Schritt zu unternehmen, nachdem es seine Pläne formell angekündigt hat. 'Nordkorea könnte den Start verzögern, wenn es Probleme mit dem Wetter oder interne Probleme gibt, aber ich sehe keinen Grund, warum sie ihn vorzeitig starten sollten', sagte Kim. US-Beamte haben erklärt, dass der Zweck des nordkoreanischen Starts möglicherweise erst bekannt wird, wenn er stattfindet. Eine Resolution des UN-Sicherheitsrates aus dem Jahr 2006 untersagte Nordkorea die Durchführung ballistischer Raketenaktivitäten. Japanische Beamte erklärten, dass sie das Objekt abschießen könnten, unabhängig davon, ob es sich um eine Rakete oder einen Satelliten handelt. 'Da die UN-Resolutionen Nordkorea die Durchführung ballistischer Raketenaktivitäten untersagen, betrachten wir dies weiterhin unter einem technischen Gesichtspunkt als Verstoß, auch wenn Nordkorea behauptet, es handele sich um einen Satelliten. Wir werden die Angelegenheit mit den beteiligten Ländern auf der Grundlage dieser Ansicht besprechen', sagte der japanische Außenminister Hirofumi Nakasone Anfang des Monats. Südkorea bekräftigte Clintons Aussagen. 'Die südkoreanische Regierung ist der Ansicht, dass es sich um eine provokative Handlung handelt, die eine ernsthafte Bedrohung für die Sicherheit Nordostasiens und der koreanischen Halbinsel darstellt, sollte Nordkorea den Start trotz kontinuierlicher Warnungen der südkoreanischen Regierung und der internationalen Gemeinschaft durchführen', sagte Außenministeriumssprecher Moon Tae-Young. 'Der Start der Langstreckenrakete ist ein klarer Verstoß gegen die Resolution Nr. 1718 des UN-Sicherheitsrates, und wir fordern Nordkorea dringend auf, solche Maßnahmen unverzüglich einzustellen.' Es wird angenommen, dass die nordkoreanische Taepodong-2-Rakete eine Reichweite von etwa 6.700 Kilometern (4.200 Meilen) hat, die es ihr, falls zutreffend, ermöglichen würde, Alaska oder Hawaii zu treffen. Pam Benson von CNN hat zu diesem Bericht beigetragen.

article_content: Following a visit to a Sri Lankan displacement camp and an aerial survey of the former civil war's final battleground, U.N. Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon described the conditions as 'shocking'. The visit took place on Saturday. Ban Ki-moon, after touring a displacement camp, remarked, 'In my extensive travels, I've encountered similar situations, but these are the most appalling scenes I've witnessed.' He expressed deep empathy for all displaced individuals. After speaking with displaced people and learning about the insufficient supplies of water and medicine, Ban appealed for improved humanitarian assistance. Ban's visit to Manik Farm, a large camp for internally displaced people in northern Sri Lanka, occurred shortly after Sri Lanka announced its triumph in a 25-year conflict against the Tamil Tigers. Aid groups and U.N. estimates suggest that approximately 250,000 to 300,000 people in Sri Lanka are refugees. Some camp residents, having endured intense combat recently, recounted their doubts about surviving. Ban conveyed to CNN's Sara Sidner, 'I have observed complete destruction, and undoubtedly, numerous civilians were caught in the crossfire.' The Sri Lankan government, however, asserts that few civilians were harmed or killed during the conflict. While some celebrated the war's conclusion, the U.N. and humanitarian organizations are concerned about the welfare of those displaced. Ban arrived in Sri Lanka on Friday, offering assistance and collaboration. In a written statement on Friday, Ban stated, 'I trust my presence will initiate a process of national recovery, renewal, and reconciliation for all Sri Lankans. That is my purpose here.' Ban engaged with Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa, requesting that humanitarian organizations receive unrestricted access to better assist displaced populations. Ban noted that the president appeared receptive to this request. Ban previously indicated he would urge the government to accelerate the vetting and processing of refugees and ensure that the displacement camps have adequate food, medical supplies, and drinking water. Sara Sidner of CNN contributed to this report.
translated_content: Nach einem Besuch in einem sri-lankischen Vertriebenenlager und einem Luftbild des ehemaligen Bürgerkriegsgebiets beschrieb UN-Generalsekretär Ban Ki-moon die Zustände als 'erschütternd'. Der Besuch fand am Samstag statt. Nach einem Rundgang durch ein Vertriebenenlager bemerkte Ban Ki-moon: 'Auf meinen zahlreichen Reisen habe ich ähnliche Situationen gesehen, aber dies sind die entsetzlichsten Zustände, die ich je erlebt habe.' Er drückte tiefes Mitgefühl für alle Vertriebenen aus. Nach Gesprächen mit Vertriebenen über die unzureichende Versorgung mit Wasser und Medikamenten forderte Ban mehr humanitäre Hilfe. Bans Besuch in Manik Farm, einem großen Lager für Binnenvertriebene im Norden Sri Lankas, erfolgte kurz nach der Erklärung Sri Lankas über den Sieg in dem 25-jährigen Konflikt gegen die Tamil Tigers. Schätzungen von Hilfsorganisationen und der UN zufolge gibt es in Sri Lanka etwa 250.000 bis 300.000 Flüchtlinge. Einige Lagerbewohner, die vor kurzem heftige Kämpfe erlebt hatten, berichteten, dass sie kaum an ihr Überleben glaubten. Ban sagte gegenüber Sara Sidner von CNN: 'Ich habe eine vollständige Zerstörung gesehen, und zweifellos sind viele Zivilisten ins Kreuzfeuer geraten.' Die sri-lankische Regierung behauptet jedoch, dass nur wenige Zivilisten während des Konflikts verletzt oder getötet wurden. Während einige das Kriegsende feierten, äußerten die UN und humanitäre Organisationen ihre Besorgnis über das Wohlergehen der Vertriebenen. Ban reiste am Freitag nach Sri Lanka und bot Hilfe und Zusammenarbeit an. In einer schriftlichen Erklärung vom Freitag sagte Ban: 'Ich hoffe, dass mein Besuch einen Prozess der nationalen Erholung, Erneuerung und Versöhnung für alle Sri Lanker anstoßen wird. Deshalb bin ich hier.' Ban traf sich mit dem sri-lankischen Präsidenten Mahinda Rajapaksa und bat darum, dass humanitäre Organisationen uneingeschränkten Zugang erhalten, um die Vertriebenen besser zu unterstützen. Ban merkte an, dass der Präsident dieser Bitte offenbar offen gegenüberstand. Ban hatte zuvor erklärt, dass er die Regierung auffordern werde, die Überprüfung und Bearbeitung von Flüchtlingen zu beschleunigen und sicherzustellen, dass die Vertriebenenlager ausreichend mit Nahrungsmitteln, Medikamenten und Trinkwasser versorgt sind. Sara Sidner von CNN hat zu diesem Bericht beigetragen.

article_content: The annual Hajj pilgrimage for Muslims began this Wednesday in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, marked by lighter crowds than usual and an unexpected deluge of rain. According to CNN's Isha Sesay, the city of Mina experienced a rare rainstorm that flooded pilgrim tents, creating challenging circumstances for the approximately 2.5 million participants. Sesay reported that the tents intended for overnight prayer and reflection were leaking and waterlogged, raising concerns about potential health risks. However, she noted that the rain, which lasted for several hours, was unlikely to deter pilgrims, many of whom had saved for years to undertake this significant religious journey. They considered it a blessing and wouldn't let the weather impede their rituals. Reports indicated no incidents among the reduced pilgrim numbers. Officials suggested that worries about swine flu might be contributing to the decline in attendance for this fifth pillar of Islam, which mandates a trip to Mecca at least once in a lifetime. Saudi's Hajj Ministry announced a 40% drop in Saudi pilgrim participation, largely attributed to disease fears. However, the number of international visitors had increased. Dr. Abdullah Al-Rabbeeah, the Saudi health minister, expressed confidence in the measures in place to monitor cases and promote awareness about self-protection against H1N1. Tragically, four pilgrims (a 17-year-old Nigerian female, a Sudanese man, an Indian man, and a Moroccan woman, each 75 years old) succumbed to the H1N1 virus during the Hajj. Many of the 2 million pilgrims arrived weeks in advance, coinciding with flu season. The five-day rituals began on Wednesday, but the drop in visitors is affecting local businesses. Fahmi al-Rashidi, a shopkeeper in Mecca's Al-Ghaza market, has decreased gold prices. Another merchant, Fahd al-Qraishi, mentioned his profit margin dropped from a typical 20% to a mere 5%. Conversely, the Hajj Ministry reported a 17% rise in international pilgrims, some of whom benefited from reduced rates at hotels like the Hilton Makkah. Finally, Khaled Nemary, a Mecca resident, stated the rainfall was the heaviest he had witnessed in 25 years. Forecasts predicted further showers through Friday. CNN's Amir Ahmed and Daniela Deane contributed to this report.

Laut Isha Sesay von CNN erlebte die Stadt Mina einen seltenen Regensturm, der die Zelte der Pilger überflutete und schwierige Bedingungen für die etwa 2,5 Millionen Teilnehmer schuf. Sesay berichtete, dass die Zelte, die für Gebet und Besinnung über Nacht gedacht waren, undicht und durchnässt waren, was Bedenken hinsichtlich potenzieller Gesundheitsrisiken aufwarf. Sie merkte jedoch an, dass der Regen, der mehrere Stunden dauerte, die Pilger wahrscheinlich nicht abschrecken würde, von denen viele jahrelang gespart hatten, um diese bedeutende religiöse Reise zu unternehmen. article_content: Dr. Conrad Murray, convicted of involuntary manslaughter in Michael Jackson's death, has shockingly accused the singer's mother of neglect. Murray claimed that 82-year-old Katherine Jackson 'failed to be there' for her son and let him down. The 59-year-old Murray lashed out when asked if he would seek forgiveness from Mrs. Jackson for administering a cocktail of drugs to the insomniac Jackson on the night of his death. He stated, 'Mrs. Jackson doesn't need to forgive me for her son's death because I am not responsible. She has nothing to forgive me for.' Murray continued, 'Instead, should anyone forgive Mrs. Jackson for failing to be the mother she could have been? Would Michael forgive his mother for her absence when he needed her?' Murray, serving a four-year sentence at Los Angeles County Jail, expressed willingness to discuss her son with Mrs. Jackson. Murray resided with the 50-year-old Jackson at his Holmy Hills mansion in Los Angeles when Jackson died on June 25, 2009. Jackson had been preparing for a major tour in Britain. During Murray's trial, evidence showed he administered drugs to Jackson and then left him unattended for extended periods while speaking with girlfriends as Jackson lay in bed. In a phone call from jail, Murray displayed no regret regarding his involvement in Jackson's death and asserted he was closer to Jackson's children—Prince, 15, Paris, 14, and Blanket, 10—than their own family. Regarding the family dispute over Jackson's £650 million will, Murray alleged in an interview with The Sun that 85-year-old Joe Jackson might be receiving funds from Katherine's allowance from the estate. Murray claimed Joe, accused of physically abusing his son, could be benefiting from Katherine's allowance. 'She probably gives funds to his father,' Murray said. 'He would be outraged if he knew Joe Jackson spent even a penny of his money.' Last month, police were summoned to Jackson's children's home in Calabasas, California, when Jackson's siblings, Janet, Randy, and Jermaine, attempted to remove them. Their brother Tito has since been appointed co-guardian. Murray maintains his innocence, claiming Jackson injected himself with Propofol, a sedative used before operations. He is kept separate from other inmates for his safety, an experience he describes as 'demoralizing.' He plans to profit from his association with Jackson by revealing further details about his famous patient. However, he stated he would not 'betray' the singer. 'One day, I will tell the entire story,' he said.

article_content: Simon Brittle, aged 45, has been sentenced to eight years in prison after a shocking incident at a motorcycle rally where he bit off his girlfriend's nose. The brutal assault, described by a judge as 'bestial,' involved Brittle biting off Heidi Smith's nose, leaving a significant and bloody injury. Brittle, from Rotherham, feigned a kiss before attacking Heidi Smith, 44, from Nottingham, causing severe bleeding. The incident occurred at the Motorcycle Action Group's Into the Valley Rally, a three-day event held in South Dalton, near Beverley in East Yorkshire. Ms. Smith was quickly taken to a hospital where surgeons used skin grafts from her hip to reconstruct her nose; however, the reconstruction left her with a visibly altered appearance. A witness, Sally Pearson, testified in Hull Crown Court that she heard Ms. Smith's screams over the rally's music as she was held down. Pearson recounted discovering the 'gaping bloody hole' where Ms. Smith's nose had been and comforted her as she called her mother to explain the attack and request assistance with her motorcycle. The court was informed that Brittle and Smith had a four-month relationship marked by instability, with Smith feeling unable to end it. Prior to the event, Brittle sent threatening messages to Smith on Facebook, indicating his violent intentions. Prosecutor Philip Evans detailed Brittle's aggressive behavior on the day of the attack, including threats to others and accusations against Smith. He further described how Brittle punched, slapped, and twisted Smith's arm before forcing her to the ground and biting her nose. Despite Smith's screams for help, onlookers initially mistook the assault for a consensual encounter. Defense barrister John Thackray acknowledged Brittle's actions as inexcusable and stated that Brittle was disgusted with himself due to his intoxication. Thackray mentioned that Brittle's life had deteriorated due to job loss, family care responsibilities, and depression. Judge Mark Bury, during sentencing, emphasized Brittle's deliberate use of his teeth as a weapon in front of Smith’s friends. In addition to the prison sentence, Brittle received an indefinite restraining order preventing him from contacting Smith. Smith has been compelled to relocate from her home of ten years because Brittle knew its location. In a victim impact statement, Smith expressed a deep sense of distrust towards men, embarrassment, and the feeling of being judged. She also noted ongoing physical issues from the assault and the inability to continue her motorcycling and skiing hobbies due to pain. Smith articulated that the incident has profoundly and irrevocably altered her life.
