article_content: The internet is facing its biggest threat ever, thanks in part to Facebook and Apple, according to the co-founder of Google. Sergey Brin stated that government attempts to control web access and the rise of increasingly 'restrictive' platforms like Facebook and Apple threaten freedom of information online. Mr. Brin also mentioned that the entertainment industry's attempts to crack down on piracy have led to the U.S. using the same technology and approach it has criticized China and Iran for using. Google co-founder Sergey Brin, pictured with co-founder Larry Page, believes governments, Apple, and Facebook are all threatening Internet freedom. Mr. Brin told The Guardian: 'There are very powerful forces that have aligned against the open Internet on all sides and around the world. I am more worried than I have been in the past. It's scary.' Mr. Brin explained that the rise of 'walled gardens' like Facebook and Apple, which tightly control what software can be released on their platforms, restricts innovation online. Both platforms have risen to become consumer giants with their own proprietary platforms which control access to their users and data. The 38-year-old told The Guardian that he and Google co-founder Larry Page could not have created their search engine if the internet was dominated by Facebook. With data stored on Facebook apps not searchable and only accessible to closed, restricted networks of users, the increasingly closed nature of the web risks stifling innovation, he said. 'There's a lot to be lost,' he said. 'For example, all the information in apps — that data is not "crawlable" by web crawlers. You can't search it.' Mr. Brin's criticism of Apple and Facebook was part of an alarming portrait he painted of the current internet landscape. He also said the original open ethos championed by internet pioneers was under threat from plans by governments to monitor web use and attempts by entertainment companies to push through new laws allowing them to demand the closure of pirate websites. Restrictive: Facebook and Apple both tightly control software on their platforms and access to their users. China has recently introduced 'real identity' rules in a bid to rein in microbloggers who have become increasingly critical of the regime, while Russian bloggers who helped foment protests against Vladimir Putin are facing increased pressure from the Kremlin. Iran is reportedly planning to introduce a sealed 'national internet' from this summer, while the UK government has announced plans to monitor citizens' use of email and social networks. Mr. Brin said five years ago he did not believe China or any country could effectively restrict the Internet for long, but he had been proven wrong. 'I thought there was no way to put the genie back in the bottle, but now it seems in certain areas the genie has been put back in the bottle,' Mr. Brin said. He cited China, Saudi Arabia, and Iran as the greatest threats. In the U.S., the entertainment industry, he said, is failing to understand that users will continue to download pirated content as long as it is easier to acquire and use than legitimately obtained material. 'I haven't tried it for many years, but when you go on a pirate website, you choose what you like, it downloads to the device of your choice, and it will just work - and then when you have to jump through all these hoops (to buy legitimate content), the walls created are disincentives for people to buy.' Some will take Mr. Brin's comments on Google rival Facebook, which has seen huge growth and now has more than 800 million members globally, with a grain of salt. The social network has announced plans for a $100 billion IPO. But his comments on increased interference by governments were echoed by Ricken Patel, co-founder of Avaaz, the 14-million strong activist network which has helped train and equip activists in Syria. Mr. Patel said: 'Governments are realizing the power of this medium to organize people, and they are trying to clamp down across the world, not just in places like China and North Korea; we're seeing bills in the United States, in Italy, all across the world.' Mr. Brin also conceded that Google has itself lost the trust of many because its servers sit on American soil, and users' data are within reach of U.S. authorities. He admitted the company was forced to hand over information to the U.S. government and was also sometimes stopped from even telling users it had done so.
translated_content: Laut dem Mitbegründer von Google steht das Internet vor seiner größten Bedrohung, auch durch Facebook und Apple. Sergey Brin erklärte, dass Regierungsversuche, den Webzugang zu kontrollieren, und der Aufstieg zunehmend 'einschränkender' Plattformen wie Facebook und Apple die Informationsfreiheit im Internet bedrohen. Herr Brin erwähnte auch, dass die Versuche der Unterhaltungsindustrie, Piraterie zu bekämpfen, dazu geführt haben, dass die USA dieselbe Technologie und denselben Ansatz verwenden, die sie zuvor an China und Iran kritisiert haben. Google-Mitbegründer Sergey Brin, zusammen mit Mitbegründer Larry Page abgebildet, ist der Ansicht, dass Regierungen, Apple und Facebook die Freiheit des Internets bedrohen. Herr Brin sagte gegenüber The Guardian: 'Es gibt sehr mächtige Kräfte, die sich auf allen Seiten der Welt gegen das offene Internet stellen. Ich bin besorgter als je zuvor. Es ist beängstigend.' Herr Brin erklärte, dass der Aufstieg von 'Walled Gardens' wie Facebook und Apple, die streng kontrollieren, welche Software auf ihren Plattformen veröffentlicht werden kann, Innovationen im Internet einschränkt. Beide Plattformen sind zu Konsumgiganten mit eigenen proprietären Plattformen geworden, die den Zugriff auf ihre Benutzer und Daten kontrollieren. Der 38-Jährige sagte gegenüber The Guardian, dass er und Google-Mitbegründer Larry Page ihre Suchmaschine nicht hätten entwickeln können, wenn das Internet von Facebook dominiert worden wäre. Da auf Facebook-Apps gespeicherte Daten nicht durchsuchbar sind und nur für geschlossene, eingeschränkte Netzwerke von Benutzern zugänglich sind, riskiert die zunehmend geschlossene Natur des Webs, Innovationen zu ersticken, sagte er. 'Es gibt viel zu verlieren', sagte er. 'Zum Beispiel sind alle Informationen in Apps – diese Daten sind für Webcrawler nicht "crawlable". Man kann sie nicht durchsuchen.' Herr Brins Kritik an Apple und Facebook war Teil eines alarmierenden Bildes, das er von der aktuellen Internetlandschaft zeichnete. Er sagte auch, dass das ursprüngliche offene Ethos, das von Internetpionieren vertreten wurde, durch Pläne von Regierungen, die Nutzung des Internets zu überwachen, und durch Versuche von Unterhaltungsunternehmen bedroht sei, neue Gesetze durchzusetzen, die es ihnen ermöglichen, die Schließung von Piraterie-Websites zu fordern. Einschränkend: Facebook und Apple kontrollieren beide streng die Software auf ihren Plattformen und den Zugriff auf ihre Benutzer. China hat kürzlich 'Echtidentitäts'-Regeln eingeführt, um Mikroblogger einzudämmen, die zunehmend Kritik am Regime üben, während russische Blogger, die zur Entstehung von Protesten gegen Wladimir Putin beigetragen haben, zunehmendem Druck aus dem Kreml ausgesetzt sind. Der Iran plant Berichten zufolge, ab diesem Sommer ein abgeriegeltes 'nationales Internet' einzuführen, während die britische Regierung Pläne zur Überwachung der E-Mail- und Social-Media-Nutzung der Bürger angekündigt hat. Herr Brin sagte vor fünf Jahren, er glaube nicht, dass China oder ein anderes Land das Internet auf Dauer wirksam einschränken könne, aber er habe sich geirrt. 'Ich dachte, es gäbe keine Möglichkeit, den Geist zurück in die Flasche zu stecken, aber jetzt scheint es, dass der Geist in einigen Bereichen wieder in die Flasche gesteckt wurde', sagte Herr Brin. Er nannte China, Saudi-Arabien und Iran als die größten Bedrohungen. In den USA, sagte er, versteht die Unterhaltungsindustrie nicht, dass Nutzer weiterhin Raubkopien herunterladen werden, solange diese einfacher zu beschaffen und zu nutzen sind als legal erworbene Materialien. 'Ich habe es seit vielen Jahren nicht mehr versucht, aber wenn man auf eine Piraterie-Website geht, wählt man aus, was man möchte, es wird auf das Gerät deiner Wahl heruntergeladen und es wird einfach funktionieren – und wenn man dann all diese Hürden überwinden muss (um legale Inhalte zu kaufen), sind die geschaffenen Mauern ein Anreiz für die Leute, nicht zu kaufen.' Einige werden Herrn Brins Kommentare zum Google-Rivalen Facebook, der ein enormes Wachstum erlebt hat und mittlerweile weltweit mehr als 800 Millionen Mitglieder hat, mit Vorsicht genießen. Das soziale Netzwerk hat Pläne für einen Börsengang im Wert von 100 Milliarden Dollar angekündigt. Aber seine Kommentare zur verstärkten Einmischung von Regierungen wurden von Ricken Patel unterstützt, dem Mitbegründer von Avaaz, dem 14 Millionen Mitglieder starken Aktivisten-Netzwerk, das zur Ausbildung und Ausrüstung von Aktivisten in Syrien beigetragen hat. Herr Patel sagte: 'Regierungen erkennen die Macht dieses Mediums, Menschen zu organisieren, und sie versuchen, auf der ganzen Welt durchzugreifen, nicht nur an Orten wie China und Nordkorea; wir sehen Gesetzesentwürfe in den Vereinigten Staaten, in Italien, auf der ganzen Welt.' Herr Brin räumte auch ein, dass Google selbst das Vertrauen vieler verloren hat, weil seine Server auf amerikanischem Boden stehen und die Daten der Nutzer in Reichweite der US-Behörden sind. Er gab zu, dass das Unternehmen gezwungen war, Informationen an die US-Regierung weiterzugeben, und ihm wurde manchmal sogar untersagt, den Nutzern mitzuteilen, dass es dies getan hatte.

article_content: Desiree Henry and Ashleigh Nelson from Great Britain are set to compete for the 100-meter gold medal on Wednesday evening. However, Asha Philip's bid for a spot in the European Championships final fell short by a mere fraction of a second. Amidst windy conditions in Zurich, both Nelson and Henry secured their places in the final by achieving second-place finishes in their respective heats. Henry, a young talent, matched her personal record of 11.21 seconds, trailing only the favored Dutch athlete Dafne Schippers, who she will face again in the final. Speaking to the BBC, the 18-year-old Henry expressed her disbelief and excitement, stating she adopted a relaxed approach, determined to enjoy the experience and is looking forward to the final. She also mentioned her training partnership with Dafne Schippers, who provides encouragement. Despite hopes for a strong British presence in the final, Philip's dreams were crushed by the narrowest of margins. The 23-year-old, along with former champion Verena Sailer and Celine Distel-Bonnet, all recorded times of 11.24 seconds. Distel-Bonnet ultimately claimed the fastest loser spot based on thousandths of a second. Philip voiced her disappointment, struggling to comprehend how she missed out on a European final spot, especially after successful performances at the Commonwealth Games and World Indoors. In the 400-meter semi-finals, world champion Christine Ohuruogu secured her place for Friday's final, finishing just ahead of Poland's Malgorzata Holub. However, Great Britain will not have any athletes competing in the men's 400-meter hurdles final, as Niall Flannery, Tom Burton, and Sebastian Rodger all failed to qualify. Despite Rodger's season's best of 49.47 seconds, he did not advance, and Ireland's Thomas Barr also missed out. There is a strong prospect of success in the men's 400m following Great Britain's dominance in the semi-finals. Conrad Williams, 32, won the first semi-final from lane eight. Martyn Rooney finished the next in 45.40 seconds, while Matthew Hudson-Smith, an exciting young athlete, achieved an even faster time to reach the final. Hudson-Smith, 19, expressed his pride in his start and noted the newness of the experience. He stated his aim has been achieved so far. Furthermore, he acknowledged that getting three British athletes into the final is a great achievement, and that a British clean sweep would be a dream scenario but that they are taking it 'one step at a time.'

article_content: Hamid Karzai, Afghanistan's outgoing president, has strongly criticized NATO's military operations, asserting that the country has only experienced suffering and loss of life as a result. Karzai also condemned NATO airstrikes as 'a violation against our sovereignty,' sparking strong reactions from various groups. The war in Afghanistan, now in its twelfth year, has resulted in the deaths of over 2,270 American soldiers and 440 British soldiers. Reacting to an airstrike in Nangarhar province on Saturday, where the Karzai government claims five civilians were killed, he criticized the military coalition's involvement in Afghanistan. 'They violate our sovereignty by conducting raids and airstrikes against our people, all in the name of fighting terrorism and under the guise of United Nations resolutions. This goes against our will,' Karzai stated. In an interview with the BBC, Karzai further criticized NATO, labeling its 12-year presence in Afghanistan as a failure. He told Newsnight, six months before leaving office, that 'the entire NATO operation caused Afghanistan a great deal of suffering, loss of life, and no real progress, as the country remains insecure.' He accused NATO of focusing their anti-terrorism efforts on Afghan villages instead of targeting Taliban and al-Qaeda bases in neighboring Pakistan. Jaap de Hoop Scheffer, former Secretary-General of NATO, countered Karzai's critique, deeming it 'unfair' to the soldiers who sacrificed their lives to protect a foreign land. 'It's unfair to the NATO soldiers who died, and to countries like Great Britain, who managed a particularly difficult area, Helmand. I've been there numerous times and deeply appreciate their efforts,' he said. 'To now say it was all a failure is unfair and I strongly disagree,' Mr de Hoop Scheffer, who led NATO for five years until 2009, added. Michael Semple, previously a deputy to the EU special representative for Afghanistan, suggested Karzai's remarks indicate he is 'out of touch with many Afghans'. 'He might believe it, but Afghans I speak with are generally polite and aware of the sacrifices made by the international mission. They prefer to express gratitude and are often appalled by the notion that it was a complete failure,' said Semple. Afghan civil society activist Orzala Ashraf Nemat described Karzai as 'very weak' for considering Taliban involvement in the Afghan government. The president dismissed concerns that including the Taliban in decision-making would negatively affect women's rights. 'I'm confident things won't revert, but I lack confidence in President Karzai's assurances,' she stated. 'My confidence stems from the dedication of Afghan women, who will likely continue to fight regardless of the circumstances,' she added. Meanwhile, the US is optimistic about finalizing an agreement with Afghanistan regarding the future of NATO troops in the country within the coming weeks. The US government aims to keep up to 10,000 troops in Afghanistan post-2014 to eliminate remaining al-Qaeda presence. However, as discussions resumed after a four-month pause, a complete disagreement remains possible. Currently, there are approximately 87,000 international troops in Afghanistan, including about 52,000 Americans. President Barack Obama stated on Friday that he would consider keeping some American forces in Afghanistan after the formal end of the conflict next year, contingent on an agreement. He acknowledged he would be comfortable with a full withdrawal of U.S. troops if no agreement is reached.
translated_content: Hamid Karzai, der scheidende Präsident Afghanistans, hat die Militäroperationen der NATO scharf kritisiert und erklärt, dass das Land dadurch nur Leid und den Verlust von Menschenleben erfahren habe. Karzai verurteilte auch die NATO-Luftangriffe als 'eine Verletzung unserer Souveränität', was heftige Reaktionen von verschiedenen Seiten auslöste. Der Krieg in Afghanistan, der sich nun im zwölften Jahr befindet, hat zum Tod von über 2.270 amerikanischen und 440 britischen Soldaten geführt. Als Reaktion auf einen Luftangriff in der Provinz Nangarhar am Samstag, bei dem die Regierung Karzai den Tod von fünf Zivilisten beklagte, kritisierte er die Beteiligung der Militärkoalition in Afghanistan. 'Sie verletzen unsere Souveränität, indem sie Razzien und Luftangriffe gegen unser Volk durchführen, alles im Namen der Terrorismusbekämpfung und unter dem Deckmantel von Resolutionen der Vereinten Nationen. Das widerspricht unserem Willen', erklärte Karzai. In einem Interview mit der BBC kritisierte Karzai die NATO weiter und bezeichnete ihre zwölfjährige Präsenz in Afghanistan als Fehlschlag. Er sagte gegenüber Newsnight, sechs Monate vor seinem Ausscheiden aus dem Amt, dass 'die gesamte NATO-Operation Afghanistan viel Leid, Verluste von Menschenleben und keinen wirklichen Fortschritt gebracht hat, da das Land weiterhin unsicher ist'. Er warf der NATO vor, ihre Bemühungen zur Terrorismusbekämpfung auf afghanische Dörfer zu konzentrieren, anstatt Taliban- und Al-Qaeda-Basen im Nachbarland Pakistan anzugreifen. Jaap de Hoop Scheffer, ehemaliger Generalsekretär der NATO, konterte Karzais Kritik und bezeichnete sie als 'unfair' gegenüber den Soldaten, die ihr Leben zum Schutz eines fremden Landes geopfert haben. 'Es ist unfair gegenüber den NATO-Soldaten, die gestorben sind, und gegenüber Ländern wie Großbritannien, die ein besonders schwieriges Gebiet, Helmand, verwaltet haben. Ich war oft dort und schätze ihre Bemühungen sehr', sagte er. 'Jetzt zu sagen, dass alles ein Misserfolg war, ist unfair, und ich bin entschieden anderer Meinung', fügte Herr de Hoop Scheffer hinzu, der die NATO fünf Jahre lang bis 2009 leitete. Michael Semple, früher stellvertretender EU-Sonderbeauftragter für Afghanistan, deutete an, dass Karzais Äußerungen darauf hindeuten, dass er 'den Kontakt zu vielen Afghanen verloren hat'. 'Er mag es glauben, aber Afghanen, mit denen ich spreche, sind im Allgemeinen höflich und sich der Opfer bewusst, die die internationale Mission gebracht hat. Sie ziehen es vor, Dankbarkeit auszudrücken, und sind oft entsetzt über die Vorstellung, dass es ein völliger Misserfolg war', sagte Semple. Die afghanische Bürgerrechtsaktivistin Orzala Ashraf Nemat bezeichnete Karzai als 'sehr schwach', weil er eine Beteiligung der Taliban an der afghanischen Regierung in Betracht zieht. Der Präsident wies Bedenken zurück, dass die Einbeziehung der Taliban in die Entscheidungsfindung negative Auswirkungen auf die Rechte der Frauen haben würde. 'Ich bin zuversichtlich, dass sich die Dinge nicht zurückentwickeln werden, aber ich habe kein Vertrauen in die Zusicherungen von Präsident Karzai', erklärte sie. 'Mein Vertrauen beruht auf dem Engagement der afghanischen Frauen, die wahrscheinlich unabhängig von den Umständen weiterkämpfen werden', fügte sie hinzu. Unterdessen sind die USA optimistisch, innerhalb der nächsten Wochen eine Einigung mit Afghanistan über die Zukunft der NATO-Truppen im Land zu erzielen. Die US-Regierung beabsichtigt, nach 2014 bis zu 10.000 Soldaten in Afghanistan zu belassen, um die verbliebene Präsenz von Al-Qaeda zu beseitigen. Da die Gespräche nach einer viermonatigen Pause jedoch wieder aufgenommen wurden, ist eine völlige Uneinigkeit weiterhin möglich. Derzeit befinden sich etwa 87.000 internationale Truppen in Afghanistan, darunter etwa 52.000 Amerikaner. Präsident Barack Obama erklärte am Freitag, er würde in Erwägung ziehen, einige amerikanische Streitkräfte nach dem formellen Ende des Konflikts im nächsten Jahr in Afghanistan zu belassen, sofern eine Einigung erzielt wird. Er räumte ein, dass er mit einem vollständigen Abzug der US-Truppen einverstanden wäre, wenn keine Einigung zustande kommt.

article_content: The rate of U.S. violent crime increased last year for the first time in nearly two decades, driven by a rise in assaults, according to the Justice Department on Wednesday. Data collected through telephone surveys by the Bureau of Justice Statistics showed a 22% increase in assaults, causing the overall violent crime rate to rise for the first time since 1993. While crime rates have generally declined, last year's increase is in contrast to the record low of 2010. Statistics indicated that the rate of assault victims increased from 19.3 to 22.5 per 1,000 people last year. These statistics encompass 3.9 million simple assaults, defined as crimes involving a threat without a weapon, resulting in relatively minor injuries. Serious violent crimes, including rape or sexual assault, robbery, and aggravated assault, are categorized separately. An estimated 1.8 million such serious incidents occurred last year; however, the increase from the previous year was statistically insignificant. The findings indicated that the number of victims in the more serious crime category increased among white and Hispanic individuals, but not among Black individuals, and among young men, but not young women. The survey included both reported and unreported crimes. Many citizens admitted to not reporting incidents to the police. Approximately half of violent crimes go unreported, according to the survey. The most closely watched annual crime statistics are scheduled for release on October 29. The FBI's Uniform Crime Report, the most closely watched report of its kind, tabulates all reported crime nationally each year. Experts anticipate that the report will show a continued decline in overall crime. A preliminary report covering the first half of 2011 suggested a decrease of about 4% in total violent crime.
translated_content: Die Rate der Gewaltverbrechen in den USA ist im vergangenen Jahr zum ersten Mal seit fast zwei Jahrzehnten gestiegen, was laut dem Justizministerium am Mittwoch auf einen Anstieg von Körperverletzungen zurückzuführen ist. Daten, die durch Telefonumfragen des Bureau of Justice Statistics erhoben wurden, zeigten einen Anstieg von Körperverletzungen um 22 %, wodurch die allgemeine Rate der Gewaltverbrechen zum ersten Mal seit 1993 anstieg. Während die Kriminalitätsraten im Allgemeinen gesunken sind, steht der Anstieg im letzten Jahr im Gegensatz zum Rekordtief des Jahres 2010. Statistiken zeigten, dass die Rate der Opfer von Körperverletzungen im vergangenen Jahr von 19,3 auf 22,5 pro 1.000 Einwohner gestiegen ist. Diese Statistiken umfassen 3,9 Millionen einfache Körperverletzungen, definiert als Verbrechen, die eine Bedrohung ohne Waffen beinhalten und zu relativ leichten Verletzungen führen. Schwere Gewaltverbrechen, einschließlich Vergewaltigung oder sexueller Nötigung, Raub und schwere Körperverletzung, werden gesondert erfasst. Schätzungsweise 1,8 Millionen solcher schwerwiegenden Vorfälle ereigneten sich im vergangenen Jahr; der Anstieg gegenüber dem Vorjahr war jedoch statistisch nicht signifikant. Die Ergebnisse zeigten, dass die Zahl der Opfer in der Kategorie der schwereren Verbrechen bei weißen und hispanischen Personen, jedoch nicht bei schwarzen Personen, und bei jungen Männern, jedoch nicht bei jungen Frauen, zugenommen hat. Die Umfrage umfasste sowohl gemeldete als auch nicht gemeldete Verbrechen. Viele Bürger gaben an, Vorfälle nicht der Polizei gemeldet zu haben. Laut der Umfrage wird etwa die Hälfte der Gewaltverbrechen nicht gemeldet. Die Veröffentlichung der am meisten beachteten jährlichen Kriminalstatistiken ist für den 29. Oktober geplant. Der Uniform Crime Report des FBI, der am meisten beachtete Bericht dieser Art, erfasst jährlich alle gemeldeten Verbrechen auf nationaler Ebene. Experten gehen davon aus, dass der Bericht einen anhaltenden Rückgang der allgemeinen Kriminalität aufzeigen wird. Ein vorläufiger Bericht, der die erste Hälfte des Jahres 2011 abdeckt, deutete auf einen Rückgang der gesamten Gewaltkriminalität um etwa 4 % hin.

article_content: A recent survey indicates that China leads the world in its population of atheists, with approximately 47% of its citizens identifying as non-believers. This figure contrasts sharply with the global average of 13%. The survey, conducted in 2012 by WIN/Gallup International, polled over 50,000 individuals across 40 countries about their religious beliefs, categorizing them as 'religious,' 'not religious,' or 'convinced atheist.' China's high atheist population is perhaps attributable to its history; the country's government, upon its formation in 1949, was officially atheist. During the Cultural Revolution (1967-1977), temples and religious artifacts were destroyed. However, religious policy has since evolved. The 1978 Constitution of the People's Republic of China guarantees 'freedom of religion' under Article 36. Despite the rise in atheist numbers globally, Pope Francis need not worry about Italy, where religious belief has increased since 2005. Chinese policy dictates that no entity or individual can force a citizen to adopt or reject a religion, nor can they discriminate based on religious belief or lack thereof. Since the mid-1980s, there has been a large-scale initiative to reconstruct Buddhist and Taoist temples. The government has shown support for Buddhism and Taoism in recent years, hosting events like the World Buddhist Forum in 2006 and the International Forum on the Daodejing in 2007. These religions are considered important aspects of Chinese culture. The state officially recognizes five religions: Buddhism, Taoism, Islam, Catholicism, and Protestantism. Yet, the survey data suggests that skepticism toward organized religion remains prevalent. In Japan, atheism remains high at 31%, possibly due to post-World War II sentiments. Surprisingly, Saudi Arabia, an Islamic country, reports 5% of its population as atheist, despite this being a punishable offense. In contrast, only 1% of the populations in Iraq and Afghanistan identify as atheist. Italy, the heart of the Catholic Church, maintains strong religious adherence, with nearly three-quarters of Italians considering themselves religious – an increase since 2005. Pope Francis recently commented that good atheists are redeemed by Jesus, urging cooperation among people of different faiths. WIN/Gallup's findings indicate that religion is most prominent among poorer and less educated populations, aligning with trends in highly religious countries such as Ghana, Nigeria, Armenia, and Fiji, where over 90% identify as religious.

article_content: For many workers, Christmas Day can feel like just another day at the office. Knowing this, some BBC employees decided to brighten their day with an impromptu dance around the Christmas tree in their newsroom. However, the staff were left embarrassed when the camera, panning through the newsroom before the headlines, captured them linking arms and dancing in Christmas hats. The footage also showed a staff member in a bear costume observing the scene. This unexpected scene made presenter Julian Worricker appear somewhat bashful as he began his news bulletin. As the camera panned to the news studio, a group of BBC staff were seen linking hands and dancing around the tree. The staff, wearing Christmas hats, danced around the Christmas tree while watched by an employee in a bear suit. While some staff remained at their desks, others joined in the impromptu celebration. The camera then focused on news presenter Julian Worricker, who looked slightly embarrassed. When the BBC first moved into their 'fish bowl' 24-hour news studio, it received complaints from viewers who spotted staff eating, chatting, and even picking their noses in the background. The BBC relocated to its new Broadcasting House, located in Portland Place and Langham Place, from its previous location in Television Centre in March 2013. The modern extension to the 1932 art-deco building was designed by architect Sir Richard MacCormac. At the time, a BBC spokesman stated: 'Our newsroom is designed to showcase the best of the BBC’s journalism and to enable teams from all platforms to work together more collaboratively and efficiently. Staff are aware that they should behave appropriately.'

article_content: In central Florida, Steven Darnell Lillie, aged 31, faces charges including third-degree felony murder and manslaughter after his baby daughter died. Authorities say she was left unattended in his truck for approximately four hours. Brevard County prosecutors formally charged Lillie on Friday. Besides murder and manslaughter, he is also charged with leaving a child under six unsupervised in a vehicle, carrying a potential 15-year prison sentence. Rockledge police investigations led to Lillie's initial charge of aggravated manslaughter, according to Florida Today. He found his daughter unresponsive in his truck around 4:45 p.m. on Monday. The infant had been strapped in her car seat inside the closed vehicle, exposed to intense sunlight, for approximately four to five hours. Witnesses reported to Channel 9 Eyewitness News that Lillie was meant to drop her off at her grandmother's before work but seemingly forgot. Lillie arrived at his workplace, the Fraternal Order of Police telemarketing office on Barton Boulevard, shortly after midday, as temperatures climbed into the high 80s. Florida Today indicates the vehicle was a black Dodge pickup. The parking lot where Lillie parked lacked shade. Eyewitness News reported that temperatures inside the truck likely soared to 100 degrees. Lieutenant Donna Seyferth of Rockledge police described the heat as 'brutal.' Lillie discovered his daughter nearly five hours later. His distressed screams alerted coworkers. During a 911 call, Lillie admitted, 'She's been in the car for hours, and I absolutely forgot about her. She's not alive.' Lieutenant Donna Seyferth told Channel 9 that officers attempted life-saving measures, as did ambulance and rescue personnel, but the child could not be revived. WKMG reported that a deviation from Lillie's normal routine led him to forget the drop-off at his daughter's grandmother's house. About four hours later, a family member inquired about the baby, prompting Lillie's discovery. Witnesses told WKMG that Lillie collapsed from distress. The baby was taken to Wuesthoff Hospital but could not be resuscitated. Lillie's attorney, Jennifer Mostert, released a statement expressing the family’s disappointment at the charges after 'the accidental death' on June 16th, 2014. She added the family has suffered an 'inconceivable loss'.

Lieutenant Donna Seyferth von der Polizei Rockledge beschrieb die Hitze als 'unerträglich'. Lillie entdeckte seine Tochter fast fünf Stunden später. Lieutenant Donna Seyferth teilte Channel 9 mit, dass die Einsatzkräfte lebensrettende Maßnahmen ergriffen, ebenso wie Rettungswagen und Notärzte, aber das Kind nicht wiederbelebt werden konnte. Etwa vier Stunden später erkundigte sich ein Familienmitglied nach dem Baby, woraufhin Lillie die schreckliche Entdeckung machte. Zeugen sagten gegenüber WKMG aus, dass Lillie vor Verzweiflung zusammenbrach. Das Baby wurde in das Wuesthoff Hospital gebracht, konnte aber nicht reanimiert werden. Lillies Anwältin, Jennifer Mostert, veröffentlichte eine Erklärung, in der sie die Enttäuschung der Familie über die Anklage nach dem 'tragischen Unfalltod' am 16. Juni 2014 zum Ausdruck brachte. Sie fügte hinzu, die Familie habe einen 'unermesslichen Verlust' erlitten.

article_content: While few would envy those with family members aboard AirAsia Flight QZ8501, Sarah Bajc offers a unique perspective. 'I'm almost a little jealous because, you know, at least they have the opportunity to find some closure,' she stated on CNN's 'New Day' on Tuesday, following the discovery of the AirAsia flight's wreckage. Her partner, Philip Woods, was a passenger on Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, which vanished nearly 10 months prior. 'We remain in limbo. There is still no evidence regarding the fate of the plane,' she said, fighting back tears. Earlier, prior to the discovery of the AirAsia flight, Bajc described experiencing a profound ache. She explained: 'It's a physical pain throughout your entire body. And just imagining what those families are feeling, I can relate. Unfortunately, I understand exactly what they're going through.' Danica Weeks, whose husband was also on MH370, shares this sentiment. The plane disappeared from radar screens on March 8 during a flight between Malaysia and China. On Sunday, AirAsia Flight QZ8501 went missing over the Java Sea en route from Surabaya, Indonesia, to Singapore, with 162 individuals on board. Debris was found in the waters off Indonesia on Tuesday. 'The past few days have been tormenting. It's brought everything back. We're reliving what we've gone through,' Weeks said. 'It's a terrible nightmare.' A support network has formed. Bajc mentioned that families of MH370 victims have united as they navigate daily life without their loved ones. Weeks emphasized the importance of AirAsia 8501 relatives seeking support. 'You just have to rely on your close friends and family,' she said. 'They are essentially the only way to cope with this.' 'After nine months, none of us are as strong as we once were.' The help center is now closed. In the weeks following MH370's disappearance, the grand ballroom at Beijing's Lido Hotel served as a briefing room for relatives of those on the flight. Families arrived daily, hoping for a miracle, but left disappointed. On Tuesday, the ballroom was dark and empty, and the family assistance center was closed. Many families feel forgotten. The search for MH370 continues. Crews are still scouring the southern Indian Ocean using advanced equipment, but no wreckage has been located. At the Malaysian government's request, Australia is leading the search. The Australian Transport Safety Bureau reported last week that seafloor mapping is ongoing, and a vessel is continuing its underwater search for the plane. 'Our work will remain thorough and methodical, so weekly progress may appear slow,' the ATSB said. 'Rest assured that our work is ongoing and aims to find MH370 as quickly as possible.' However, families of passengers and crew may face a longer wait. 'Assuming no major delays involving vessels, equipment, or weather, the current underwater search area may be largely completed around May 2015,' the ATSB stated. Weeks has no choice but to remain patient. 'We will never find peace until we honor our loved ones by bringing them home.'

article_content: Looking for Thanksgiving dinner conversation topics? The NPR team suggests these public media podcasts. Episode descriptions are sourced from podcast webpages and edited for brevity and clarity. All The Only Ones is a new 3-part series from NPR's Embedded. Host Laine Kaplan-Levenson explores the often-overlooked history of trans youth in America. This series follows young transgender people today and journeys back to the turn of the 20th century to meet some of the earliest documented trans youth in American history. Episode 1: 'The Missing Piece of the Puzzle'. Sold Out: Rethinking Housing In America returns with a new season. Host Erin Baldassari and a team of reporters examine how climate change affects our concept of home. In this episode, follow the Escutia family from the night a flood devastated their hometown through their months-long search for affordable housing on higher ground. Start listening. article_content: In Tunis, Tunisia, several hundred protesters gathered in the capital's center on Sunday, observed by riot police. Army personnel and military vehicles were deployed on the main street near the interior ministry. Police occasionally used tear gas, causing young protesters to briefly disperse before returning. Some younger protesters threw stones at the police, while older individuals in the group urged them to remain calm. On Saturday, authorities enacted an overnight curfew in the capital and surrounding areas, following a weekend of protests against the interim government and security forces, as reported by state media. The recent protests reflect increasing concerns among Tunisians that their demands for democratic governance are not being adequately addressed. Protesters are advocating for the continuation of the democratization process, significant reforms, and a return to the original principles of the Tunisian revolution. On Saturday, protesters demanded the interior minister's resignation, chanting slogans such as 'The people call for a new revolution' and 'No fear or terror, power belongs to the people,' according to Agence Tunis Afrique Presse. The authorities stated that the curfew, effective nightly from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., is intended to deter looting and safeguard citizens. Protests across Arab countries were ignited in Tunisia after an unemployed college graduate self-immolated in response to police confiscating his fruit cart, thus depriving him of his livelihood. This act triggered widespread demonstrations concerning high unemployment, governmental corruption, and political repression, ultimately leading to the departure of autocratic President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali in January. CNN's Nic Robertson contributed to this report.

article_content: Editor's note: CNN agreed not to use the full names of the family in this article out of concern for their safety. Youssif is smiling again, and his scars are healing well. Doctors are monitoring the swelling on his right ear. WOODLAND HILLS, California (CNN) -- Youssif happily removes his plastic face mask and pats his cheeks, which were once covered in severe burns. 'No hurt,' the 5-year-old Iraqi boy says in English. 'No hurt.' He then shows his right hand. It also had hardened scar tissue after he was attacked by masked men outside his home in central Baghdad on January 15, 2007. Now, his hand is smooth. Youssif flashes a proud grin. A few moments later, he runs off and returns with his kindergarten portfolio. In less than a month of school, he is now writing the alphabet in upper and lowercase. He reads a book, repeating each word after the narrator. When he gets to the word 'you,' he is tickled. He points at the name 'Youssif' and then covers the final four letters. 'You,' he says. Youssif started attending an American school just last month, exactly one year after he was attacked in Baghdad. In a recent letter to those who have helped his son, Youssif's father described the anniversary as a 'very hard day' but one that also brought joy. 'But this year, it was the day for another miracle, Youssif's first day of kindergarten. It was a very happy day,' Youssif's father said. Each day begins with Youssif's father strapping him into a bike trailer. His dad then pedals him to school. On one recent morning, his dad's mobile phone played Arabic music as Youssif quietly sat in the back, a helmet securely fastened, the wind blowing past. As soon as they arrived at the school, Youssif's slow walk away from his father, his head down, quickly turned into a sprint toward his classroom, and all that could be seen was the big red 'S' on his Superman backpack flying away. 'Harry,' Youssif says in a small, muffled voice, reading the writing on the dry-erase board after getting help from classmates seated on the rug. He then receives a congratulatory high-five from one of his kindergarten teachers. Youssif is adjusting well to school, able to write out the alphabet and count to 12 without hesitation. He always finishes with an accomplished sigh, wide eyes, and a smile so big, it's as if he is compensating for the 10 months he couldn't smile. He quickly shows the pencil box on his desk, pointing to his name written on it and then pointing to himself with the same tiny finger and nodding, letting you know that it is his. 'The kids love Youssif. They get more excited than he does when he learns a new word in English, and they brag about it for hours,' the mother of a classmate says. Youssif is attending the school thanks to assistance from the Children's Burn Foundation, the Grossman Burn Center, and hundreds of thousands of dollars donated by CNN.com users to help bring him and his family to the United States for treatment. Youssif has undergone more than half a dozen surgeries. One removed the most significant scarring, which stretched about half a foot, from one of his ears to below his chin. He may undergo as many as 12 more procedures, his doctors say, mostly to refine the scars. His right ear has swelled, and doctors are monitoring it to determine the best way to manage it. He wears a clear plastic face mask for much of the day to keep his skin tight and help it heal correctly. But the young boy's transformation -- both physically and emotionally -- is truly remarkable. Back at his apartment, Youssif peels a clementine. He uses exaggerated motions as he puts each section in his mouth. At one point, he places his hand on his hip and taps his foot, waiting for someone to acknowledge his accomplishment. When he came to America in September, he couldn't eat -- or at least not like this. He smiles again. 'Now, Youssif eats anything he wants, because he can open and close his mouth,' his father said in the letter. 'I have begun to see my son's lively spirit return. The surgeries have removed more than just external scars; they are also beginning to remove his internal scars.' 'A few weeks ago we went to the park, and Youssif rode on the merry-go-round. Every time he passed by, he shrieked and laughed and waved wildly to me. I thought my heart would burst with happiness.'

WOODLAND HILLS, Kalifornien (CNN) – Fröhlich nimmt Youssif seine Gesichtsmaske aus Plastik ab und tätschelt seine Wangen, die einst von schweren Verbrennungen bedeckt waren. ‘Kein Schmerz’, sagt der 5-jährige irakische Junge auf Englisch. ‘Kein Schmerz.’ Dann zeigt er seine rechte Hand. Auch sie war von hartem Narbengewebe bedeckt, nachdem er am 15. Januar 2007 vor seinem Haus in Zentral-Bagdad von maskierten Männern angegriffen worden war. Jetzt ist seine Hand glatt. Youssif strahlt stolz. Kurz darauf rennt er los und kommt mit seiner Kindergartenmappe zurück. Nach weniger als einem Monat in der Schule schreibt er nun das Alphabet in Groß- und Kleinbuchstaben. Er liest in einem Buch und spricht jedes Wort dem Erzähler nach. Beim Wort ‘you’ muss er kichern. Er zeigt auf seinen Namen ‘Youssif’ und verdeckt die letzten vier Buchstaben. ‘You’, sagt er. Youssif besucht seit letztem Monat eine amerikanische Schule, genau ein Jahr nach dem Angriff in Bagdad. In einem Brief an alle Helfer seines Sohnes beschreibt Youssifs Vater diesen Jahrestag als einen ‘sehr schweren Tag’, der aber auch Freude brachte. ‘Doch dieses Jahr war es der Tag eines weiteren Wunders: Youssifs erster Tag im Kindergarten. Es war ein sehr glücklicher Tag’, schrieb Youssifs Vater. Jeden Morgen schnallt Youssifs Vater ihn in einen Fahrradanhänger. Dann fährt er ihn zur Schule. An einem Morgen spielte das Handy seines Vaters arabische Musik, während Youssif mit festgeschnalltem Helm still hinten sass und der Wind an ihm vorbeizog. An der Schule angekommen, wechselte Youssifs langsames Weggehen von seinem Vater mit gesenktem Kopf schnell in einen Sprint zu seinem Klassenzimmer, wobei nur noch das große rote ‘S’ auf seinem Superman-Rucksack zu sehen war. ‘Harry’, sagt Youssif leise und undeutlich, als er nach etwas Hilfe von seinen Klassenkameraden auf dem Teppich die Schrift auf der Whiteboard vorliest. Dann bekommt er ein anerkennendes High-Five von einer seiner Erzieherinnen. Youssif findet sich gut in der Schule zurecht, kann das Alphabet schreiben und ohne Zögern bis 12 zählen. Er beendet das immer mit einem zufriedenen Seufzer, großen Augen und einem so breiten Lächeln, als würde er die 10 Monate nachholen, in denen er nicht lächeln konnte. Schnell zeigt er sein Federmäppchen auf dem Tisch, deutet auf seinen Namen darauf und dann mit demselben kleinen Finger auf sich selbst, nickt und zeigt so, dass es ihm gehört. ‘Die Kinder lieben Youssif. Sie freuen sich noch mehr als er, wenn er ein neues englisches Wort lernt, und prahlen stundenlang damit’, sagt die Mutter eines Klassenkameraden. Youssif besucht die Schule dank der Unterstützung der Children's Burn Foundation, des Grossman Burn Center und der Hunderttausenden von Dollar, die von CNN.com-Nutzern gespendet wurden, um ihm und seiner Familie die Behandlung in den Vereinigten Staaten zu ermöglichen. Youssif hat bereits mehr als ein halbes Dutzend Operationen hinter sich. Bei einer wurde die schlimmste Narbe entfernt, die sich etwa eine halbe Fußlänge von einem seiner Ohren bis unter sein Kinn zog. Laut seinen Ärzten muss er sich möglicherweise bis zu 12 weiteren Eingriffen unterziehen, hauptsächlich zur Verfeinerung der Narben. Sein rechtes Ohr ist angeschwollen, und die Ärzte überwachen es, um die beste Behandlungsmethode zu finden. Er trägt fast den ganzen Tag eine durchsichtige Plastikmaske, um seine Haut zu straffen und die Heilung zu unterstützen. Aber die Verwandlung des Jungen – sowohl körperlich als auch seelisch – ist wirklich bemerkenswert. Zurück in seiner Wohnung schält Youssif eine Mandarine. Er macht übertriebene Bewegungen, als er jedes Segment in den Mund steckt. Dann stemmt er die Hände in die Hüften und tippt mit dem Fuß, um für seine Leistung gelobt zu werden. Als er im September nach Amerika kam, konnte er so nicht essen. Er lächelt wieder. ‘Jetzt isst Youssif alles, was er will, weil er seinen Mund öffnen und schließen kann’, schrieb sein Vater. ‘Ich sehe den lebhaften Geist meines Sohnes zurückkehren. Die Operationen haben nicht nur äußere Narben entfernt, sondern beginnen auch, seine inneren Narben zu heilen.’ ‘Vor ein paar Wochen waren wir im Park, und Youssif ist Karussell gefahren. Jedes Mal, wenn er vorbeikam, hat er gekreischt, gelacht und mir wild zugewunken. Ich dachte, mein Herz platzt vor Glück!’

article_content: The aftermath of Adam Lambert's controversial American Music Awards performance continues, with 'Good Morning America' canceling the singer's scheduled live performance for Wednesday morning. ABC received over 1,500 complaints regarding the performance and notified potential concert attendees that Lambert's appearance was canceled. According to a network spokesperson, the decision was due to concerns about broadcasting a similar performance so early in the morning, referencing Lambert's prior AMAs performance. Rival network CBS's 'The Early Show' quickly announced that Lambert would appear on their program to perform and address the controversy on Wednesday morning. Lambert's performance at the AMAs included sexually suggestive dance sequences and a kiss with his male keyboardist, drawing criticism from viewers. The Parents Television Council, a media watchdog group, also condemned the show as vulgar, urging its members to contact ABC, Dick Clark Productions, and the show's advertisers to voice their concerns. The PTC stated on their website that the 'American Music Awards' broadcast was 'tasteless and vulgar,' highlighting Lambert's simulated oral sex act and 'demeaning behavior'. Melissa Henson, director of communications and public education for the PTC, clarified that the council's concern was with the simulated act, not the same-sex kiss. 'The gender has nothing to do with it,' Henson said. 'It would be true if a woman's face was thrust into his crotch.' Henson added that the council would not have objected to Lambert performing on 'Good Morning America' if he kept the performance 'clean'.

article_content: Prime Minister David Cameron aimed to dispel 'myths' surrounding the jobs market, asserting that most new jobs are now well-paid and full-time. Cameron proclaimed Britain as the 'jobs factory of Europe', vowing that a Conservative government would elevate employment to unparalleled levels. He sought to 'bust myths' about the jobs market, emphasizing the prevalence of well-paid, full-time positions among new hires. However, he conceded that he would fail to meet his pledge to curb migration, attributing it to Britain's thriving job market attracting migrants. During a speech in Ipswich, Cameron announced a target of 'full employment' for Britain, surpassing all other G7 nations. The UK currently holds fourth place at 72 percent, trailing Canada and Japan, with Germany leading at 74 percent. He noted that, in the past year, 9 out of 10 individuals securing employment found full-time positions. Cameron acknowledged the 'tough few years' for the UK economy but stated that the country was 'emerging stronger', urging voters to maintain their support. 'Full employment, while an economic term, translates to the security of a regular wage for more citizens, benefiting individuals, families, and children through job opportunities,' Cameron stated. 'As a nation, we have faced challenges, but we are now recovering. We are the jobs factory of Europe, generating more jobs than the rest of Europe combined. This is the essence of our long-term plan, and a Conservative vote ensures we continue on this path to recovery.' The Prime Minister outlined five key Conservative commitments for the next Parliament. Cameron directly appealed to small businesses, emphasizing the Conservative party's support. 'The Conservatives champion small businesses, from roofers and retailers to builders and businesswomen. We support those who take risks, create wealth, and generate jobs in our country.' 'These are the people we admire and want to assist. While other parties may talk about it, we deliver,' he said. Britain currently ranks fourth among G7 nations for employment; Cameron aims to surpass Germany, Japan, and Canada. article_content: 'Yesterday, Darek Fidyka, a fireman, shared his story of how he was tragically paralyzed from the waist down after being stabbed multiple times by a jealous ex-husband of his then-girlfriend. The incident occurred when Fidyka tried to intervene to stop the man from vandalizing his car. This devastating attack left Fidyka, then 40, unable to move his legs. However, he has since regained the ability to walk thanks to an innovative British medical procedure. Fidyka recounted to the Mail, 'He stabbed me 18 times. It was a premeditated ambush with a knife.' Despite the severity of his injuries, including a severed spinal cord, Fidyka is now walking again, marking him as potentially the first person to recover from such extensive spinal damage. Following the July 2010 attack, Fidyka faced the prospect of life in a wheelchair, with no sensation or movement below the waist. Yet, recent headlines celebrated his remarkable progress: two years after undergoing a groundbreaking treatment in Britain, he can walk again. This recovery has allowed him to resume his passion for hunting and drive a specially adapted vehicle. Born in Bulgaria, Fidyka worked as a painter, decorator, and volunteer fireman in Poland before the attack. He describes his recovery as a rebirth. As he explained in an interview for the BBC Panorama program 'To Walk Again,' regaining movement felt like starting life anew. The pioneering procedure involved transplanting cells from Fidyka's nose to the injured section of his spinal cord to repair the damage. After extensive physiotherapy, he began to feel sensation in his legs. This treatment, supported by the Nicholls Spinal Injury Foundation and the UK Stem Cell Foundation, offers hope to millions affected by paralysis. The surgery was performed by neurosurgeons in Wroclaw, Poland. Professor Geoffrey Raisman, whose team at University College London developed the technique, noted that Fidyka's injury presented an ideal opportunity to test the procedure on a human. However, Dr. Dusko Ilic of King's College London advised caution, noting that while some animal studies showed significant improvement with olfactory ensheathing glial (OEG) cell transplants, others did not. He emphasized the need for larger-scale studies to determine the treatment's reliability. Professor Raisman's work is potentially revolutionary. If his surgery proves to be a lasting solution for spinal injuries, he could be recognized alongside medical pioneers like Christiaan Barnard and Sir Robert Edwards. For now, his successful treatment of Darek Fidyka provides hope for many with spinal cord injuries. Raisman is known for his unconventional approach. He is described by colleagues as a dedicated, meticulous researcher who has focused on neuron regeneration. Born into a working-class family in 1939, he overcame obstacles to excel in his field. His early discovery of the brain's plasticity challenged established beliefs that brain and spinal cord damage was irreversible. David Nicholls, whose son Daniel was paralyzed in a diving accident, played a crucial role in funding this research. Doctors initially told Nicholls that his son had no chance of recovery, but he remained determined to find a cure. He raised £1 million through fundraising to support research into spinal injuries. This funding enabled surgeons in Wroclaw to treat Fidyka, who had a completely severed spinal cord. After the surgery, Fidyka regained the ability to walk with assistance and resume his hobbies. Nicholls now hopes his son will be considered for the same treatment, driven by his promise to find a cure. Nicholls established the Nicholls Spinal Injury Foundation to continue raising funds for medical research after witnessing his son's devastating accident.

article_content: By Stuart Woledge. PUBLISHED: 04:40 EST, 30 August 2013 | UPDATED: 07:30 EST, 30 August 2013. Students aren't typically known for keeping their accommodations pristine. Mould often grows in fridges, and bins overflow with half-eaten kebabs and empty cider cans. So, it's perhaps fitting that this year's ugliest building award has been given to the new University College London residence at 465 Caledonian Road, which judges 'struggled to see as fit for human habitation'. Described as a 'Frankenstein concoction,' it beat out runner-up Castle Mill – also student accommodation – which has angered residents by obscuring postcard views of Oxford's dreaming spires. Grim: The UCL student accommodation at 465 Caledonian Road was initially refused planning permission, but a planning inspector overruled the decision. Room with a view: The windows of the new property are at a different level than the original facade, meaning students face a brick wall. Public anger is such that calls have been made for a judicial review of the approval process. However, 465 Caledonian Road in the London Borough of Islington won Building Design magazine's Carbuncle Cup for the worst new building of 2013. Described as an 'outrageous housing scheme,' 465 Caledonian Road offered 'deep grounds for offense in its cavalier attitude to a historic asset,' according to the jury. Mind the gap: The developer retained the original frontage but demolished the rest of the Victorian building to make way for the new construction. The magazine accused the architect, Stephen George & Partners, of knowing 'a thing or two about grotesque overdevelopment,' adding: 'The practice’s solution in Islington has to rank as the mother of all facadectomies.' Stephen George declined to comment. The new development was built on a site formerly occupied by a listed warehouse dating back to 1874. All but the front facade was torn down for the new building. The retained facade was stripped of its windows and positioned 2m in front of the replacement building. However, the retained openings don't align with the new windows, leaving occupants with a brick wall view. According to Building Design: 'Of the 44 student rooms addressing Caledonian Road, over half lack eye-level outlooks.' To compensate for the fact that the new building was two storeys higher than the original, the builder removed the top of the old facade, added a new floor, and reattached the original top. Building Design said: 'One might hope that these compromised rooms represent the worst the development has to offer, but many of those facing away from the street promise to be even grimmer.' When Islington council denied planning permission in 2009, it identified 151 units as 'suffering from poor outlook', 179 as not receiving 'good daylighting', and 60 as not having 'adequate privacy'. Controversial: Oxford University's Castle Mill student accommodation was narrowly defeated by Caledonian Road. Some rooms face each other from windows just 5m apart. Building Design noted that residents of Pentonville Prison have a better view. Overturning the council's decision, the Planning Inspectorate wrote: 'There is agreement that the nature of the accommodation warrants some departure from the amenity standards that would be applied to residential accommodation intended for normal domestic occupation.' 'Relevant factors in this are that individual students would occupy the accommodation for less than a year, and that its main function would be for sleeping due to intensive daytime activities taking place at the university campus.' Characterless: The Avant Garde building on Bethnal Green Road (left), which critics say fails to blend into the Victorian surroundings. Right, the Redcar Beacon. 'The dumpster': The stark-looking Porth Eirias Watersports Centre in Colwyn Bay, Wales, is part of a multi-million pound seafront redevelopment, but its skip-like shape has earned it an unfortunate nickname. 'Lumpen': The 234-room Premier Inn on York Road in Waterloo, designed by Hamiltons, is the third London building to make the Carbuncle Cup shortlist; Building Design describes it as a 'travesty'.

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- The U.S. military has tried to close the security gaps that it believes allowed a military intelligence analyst to steal hundreds of thousands of classified documents and ultimately provide them to the WikiLeaks website. Since the first batch of documents was published, military officials have warned about the need to balance security and limited access with the need for troops around the world to access the latest intelligence. 'In the wake of this incident, it will be a real challenge to strike the right balance between security and providing our frontline troops with the information they need,' former Defense Secretary Robert Gates said after WikiLeaks published a trove of documents about the war in Afghanistan. 'We want soldiers in a forward operating base to have all the information that impacts their security and their ability to accomplish their mission.' Following the WikiLeaks publications, Gates ordered two reviews of document security, according to Pentagon spokesman Bryan Whitman. As a result, stricter rules and more restrictive technology have been implemented to help close the gaps while maintaining that balance, he said. 'Bottom line: It is now much more difficult for a determined actor to access and move information outside of authorized channels,' Whitman wrote in an e-mail to reporters on Sunday. In the short term, Whitman said computers within the Department of Defense classified system have been disabled from recording and downloading information, 'as a temporary technical solution to mitigate the future risks of personnel moving classified data to unclassified systems.' The ability to access classified information was established after the September 11, 2001, attacks as a way to promote intra-agency cooperation. Known in the government as Net-Centric Diplomacy, the initiative aimed to give those on the front lines a full range of details from diplomatic and military communications. Pfc. Bradley Manning is charged with exploiting this system to download documents and provide them to WikiLeaks. Manning, a U.S. soldier who served in Iraq, has been charged with illegally transferring classified data onto his personal computer and adding unauthorized software to a classified computer system. The 22-year-old is suspected of having downloaded thousands of other documents from a server in Iraq. Manning is currently being held by the military in Quantico, Virginia, awaiting trial. According to the charges against him, he was able to download documents for which he had clearance and also gain access to information that 'knowingly exceeded his authorized access.' The Defense Department also has restricted the number of systems where data can be moved from a classified computer to an unclassified computer, and now requires two people to move data 'to ensure proper oversight and reduce chances of unauthorized release of classified material.' The Pentagon is developing methods to monitor suspicious behavior, 'similar to procedures now being used by credit card companies to detect and monitor fraud,' Whitman explained. Still, some changes have yet to be installed system-wide. A monitoring system to alert to unusual access of data is currently overseeing 60 percent of the classified system, according to Whitman, although the installation of the monitoring system is being accelerated. The Pentagon also has increased training to make staff more aware of the 'insider threat,' Whitman said.
translated_content: Washington (CNN) – Das US-Militär hat versucht, die Sicherheitslücken zu schließen, die es nach eigener Einschätzung einem Militärgeheimdienstanalysten ermöglichten, Hunderttausende von geheimen Dokumenten zu stehlen und sie letztendlich an die WikiLeaks-Website weiterzugeben. Seit der Veröffentlichung der ersten Dokumentensammlung haben Militärbeamte vor der Notwendigkeit gewarnt, Sicherheit und eingeschränkten Zugang mit dem Bedürfnis der Truppen auf der ganzen Welt, auf die neuesten Informationen zuzugreifen, in Einklang zu bringen. 'Nach diesem Vorfall wird es eine echte Herausforderung sein, das richtige Gleichgewicht zwischen Sicherheit und der Bereitstellung der Informationen, die unsere Truppen an vorderster Front benötigen, zu finden', sagte der ehemalige Verteidigungsminister Robert Gates, nachdem WikiLeaks eine Sammlung von Dokumenten über den Krieg in Afghanistan veröffentlicht hatte. 'Wir wollen, dass Soldaten in einem vorgeschobenen Einsatzstützpunkt alle Informationen haben, die ihre Sicherheit und ihre Fähigkeit, ihre Mission zu erfüllen, beeinträchtigen.' Nach den WikiLeaks-Veröffentlichungen ordnete Gates laut Pentagon-Sprecher Bryan Whitman zwei Überprüfungen der Dokumentsicherheit an. Infolgedessen wurden strengere Regeln und restriktivere Technologien implementiert, um die Lücken zu schließen und gleichzeitig dieses Gleichgewicht aufrechtzuerhalten, sagte er. 'Unterm Strich ist es jetzt viel schwieriger für eine Einzelperson mit krimineller Energie, auf Informationen zuzugreifen und diese außerhalb der autorisierten Kanäle zu bewegen', schrieb Whitman am Sonntag in einer E-Mail an Reporter. Kurzfristig, so Whitman, wurde bei Computern innerhalb des klassifizierten Systems des Verteidigungsministeriums die Möglichkeit deaktiviert, Informationen aufzuzeichnen und herunterzuladen, 'als vorübergehende technische Lösung, um die zukünftigen Risiken zu mindern, dass Personal klassifizierte Daten in unklassifizierte Systeme verschiebt.' Die Möglichkeit, auf klassifizierte Informationen zuzugreifen, wurde nach den Anschlägen vom 11. September 2001 eingerichtet, um die Zusammenarbeit zwischen den Behörden zu fördern. Die Initiative, die in der Regierung als Net-Centric Diplomacy bekannt ist, zielte darauf ab, denjenigen an der Front eine vollständige Palette von Details aus diplomatischen und militärischen Kommunikationen zu geben. Pfc. Bradley Manning wird beschuldigt, dieses System ausgenutzt zu haben, um Dokumente herunterzuladen und sie an WikiLeaks weiterzugeben. Manning, ein US-Soldat, der im Irak gedient hat, wird beschuldigt, illegal klassifizierte Daten auf seinen persönlichen Computer übertragen und nicht autorisierte Software auf ein klassifiziertes Computersystem aufgespielt zu haben. Der 22-Jährige steht im Verdacht, Tausende weiterer Dokumente von einem Server im Irak heruntergeladen zu haben. Manning wird derzeit vom Militär in Quantico, Virginia, inhaftiert und wartet auf seinen Prozess. Laut den Anklagen gegen ihn konnte er Dokumente herunterladen, für die er eine Genehmigung hatte, und auch auf Informationen zugreifen, die 'wissentlich seine autorisierten Zugriffsrechte überschritten'. Das Verteidigungsministerium hat auch die Anzahl der Systeme eingeschränkt, auf denen Daten von einem klassifizierten Computer auf einen unklassifizierten Computer verschoben werden können, und benötigt nun zwei Personen, um Daten zu verschieben, 'um eine ordnungsgemäße Aufsicht zu gewährleisten und die Wahrscheinlichkeit einer unbefugten Freigabe von klassifiziertem Material zu verringern'. Das Pentagon entwickelt Methoden zur Überwachung verdächtigen Verhaltens, 'ähnlich den Verfahren, die derzeit von Kreditkartenunternehmen zur Erkennung und Überwachung von Betrug eingesetzt werden', erklärte Whitman. Dennoch müssen einige Änderungen noch systemweit installiert werden. Ein Überwachungssystem, das vor ungewöhnlichem Zugriff auf Daten warnt, überwacht derzeit 60 Prozent des klassifizierten Systems, so Whitman, obwohl die Installation des Überwachungssystems beschleunigt wird. Das Pentagon hat auch die Schulung verstärkt, um die Mitarbeiter stärker für die 'Gefahr durch Innentäter' zu sensibilisieren, sagte Whitman.

article_content: The £10 million Iraq War inquiry is likely to be delayed until after the next general election due to ongoing disagreements within Whitehall regarding which documents can be published. Sources within Whitehall indicate that the inquiry's chief, Sir John Chilcot, continues to request the declassification of documents from civil servants, suggesting the report is still incomplete. Furthermore, legal letters outlining potential criticisms have not yet been dispatched to key individuals such as Tony Blair and Alastair Campbell. To the disappointment of the families of the 179 British soldiers who died in the conflict, the complete transcripts of phone calls and letters exchanged between George W. Bush and Tony Blair will not be included in Chilcot's final report. The report is anticipated to be critical of the actions taken by prominent Labour figures in the lead-up to the Iraq War. These revelations significantly diminish hopes that the inquiry, which commenced in 2009, would release its report before the general election scheduled for next May. Cabinet Secretary Sir Jeremy Heywood reportedly cautioned the inquiry that the report, which is expected to be critical of Mr Blair and other senior Labour figures, should be published by the end of January to avoid influencing the election. An absolute deadline of early March was allegedly set, after which the report would be postponed to prevent it from becoming a political issue during the election campaign. This development will disappoint the families of the 179 British soldiers killed in the conflict, who have been waiting for years to learn the true reasons for their deployment to war. Some have already labeled the inquiry a ‘whitewash’ following the announcement that full details of 25 letters sent by Mr Blair to George W. Bush, as well as transcripts of 130 phone calls between the two leaders, will not be disclosed. Sir John Chilcot's inquiry, initiated in 2009, is still believed to be several months away from publication. Reportedly, Mr Blair assured the US President of his unconditional support for the war, stating, ‘You know, George, whatever you decide to do, I’m with you.’ Sir Jeremy decided in May of this year that only the ‘gist’ of these conversations could be published. This agreement, reached after two and a half years of negotiations, was initially viewed as a breakthrough that could finally lead to the report's publication. However, to the dismay of some within Whitehall, Sir John has continued to request the release of sensitive information, with each request requiring weeks for consideration. There is also increasing speculation that Sir John is finding it difficult to reconcile the differing opinions of the inquiry panel members on crucial matters, suggesting that his report might not be finalized for several months. A spokesman for the inquiry confirmed that the legal process, in which individuals like Mr Blair will have the opportunity to respond to criticisms, has not yet commenced. This process is projected to last at least two months and must be completed before the report can be released. Sir Jeremy acknowledged last week that there had been a ‘delay of sorts’ while thousands of requests to declassify documents were being reviewed. However, he insisted that there would be no cover-up. When giving evidence to MPs, he stated: ‘I am absolutely confident that the report will be as transparent as it needs to be. I can understand people’s frustration, but I think the report will be more transparent than you are expecting, and I don’t think in any shape or form it can be called a cover-up.’ June 15, 2009: Prime Minister Gordon Brown announces an inquiry led by Sir John Chilcot ‘to consider the period from the summer of 2001 to the end of July 2009, encompassing the lead-up to the conflict in Iraq, the military action, and its aftermath.’ November 24, 2009: First public hearings held. January 29, 2010: Tony Blair provides evidence, stating he has no regrets about removing Saddam. He is met with boos upon his departure. February 2, 2011: Final public hearing takes place. Former foreign secretary Jack Straw states that the UK never had a policy of regime change. November 16, 2011: The report’s release is postponed until at least the summer of 2012 following a disagreement with the Cabinet Office regarding the use of classified documents, including Mr Blair’s private messages to President Bush in the run-up to the war. July 16, 2012: Sir John announces that the report will not be published before mid-2013 because no decision has been reached on which documents should be released. November 7, 2013: Sir John suggests that publication could be delayed indefinitely due to a dispute over 130 new transcripts of conversations between Brown, Blair, and Bush. May 16, 2014: David Cameron expresses hope for publication by the end of the year. May 27, 2014: Mr Blair maintains that he is not responsible for the delay, stating that he wishes to hear the findings so that he can defend himself. May 29, 2014: An agreement is reached to publish extracts of exchanges between Blair and Bush – but the full texts will remain confidential. September 14, 2014: Whitehall sources report that Sir John is still requesting classified documents from civil servants, and legal letters to key Labour figures are yet to be sent. It is now unlikely that the report will be published before the 2015 General Election.

Quellen in Whitehall deuten darauf hin, dass der Leiter der Untersuchung, Sir John Chilcot, weiterhin die Freigabe von Dokumenten von Beamten beantragt, was darauf hindeutet, dass der Bericht noch unvollständig ist. Darüber hinaus wurden juristische Schreiben, in denen mögliche Kritikpunkte aufgeführt sind, noch nicht an Schlüsselfiguren wie Tony Blair und Alastair Campbell versandt. Zur Enttäuschung der Familien der 179 britischen Soldaten, die in dem Konflikt gestorben sind, werden die vollständigen Transkripte von Telefongesprächen und Briefen zwischen George W. Bush und Tony Blair nicht in Chilcots Abschlussbericht enthalten sein. Es wird erwartet, dass der Bericht die Maßnahmen prominenter Labour-Politiker im Vorfeld des Irak-Kriegs kritisiert. Diese Enthüllungen schmälern die Hoffnung erheblich, dass die Untersuchung, die 2009 begann, ihren Bericht vor den für nächsten Mai geplanten Parlamentswahlen veröffentlichen würde. Zum Entsetzen einiger in Whitehall hat Sir John jedoch weiterhin die Freigabe sensibler Informationen beantragt, wobei jeder Antrag Wochen zur Prüfung benötigt. Es gibt auch zunehmend Spekulationen darüber, dass es Sir John schwerfällt, die unterschiedlichen Meinungen der Mitglieder des Untersuchungsausschusses zu entscheidenden Fragen in Einklang zu bringen, was darauf hindeutet, dass sein Bericht möglicherweise erst in einigen Monaten fertiggestellt wird. Ein Sprecher der Untersuchung bestätigte, dass das Gerichtsverfahren, in dem Personen wie Mr. Blair die Möglichkeit haben werden, auf Kritik zu reagieren, noch nicht begonnen hat. Es wird erwartet, dass dieser Prozess mindestens zwei Monate dauert und abgeschlossen sein muss, bevor der Bericht veröffentlicht werden kann. Sir Jeremy räumte letzte Woche ein, dass es eine 'Art Verzögerung' gegeben hat, während Tausende von Anträgen auf Freigabe von Dokumenten geprüft wurden. Er bestand jedoch darauf, dass es keine Vertuschung geben werde. Als er vor den Abgeordneten aussagte, erklärte er: 'Ich bin absolut zuversichtlich, dass der Bericht so transparent sein wird, wie er sein muss. Ich kann die Frustration der Menschen verstehen, aber ich denke, der Bericht wird transparenter sein, als Sie erwarten, und ich glaube nicht, dass er in irgendeiner Weise als Vertuschung bezeichnet werden kann.' 15. Juni 2009: Premierminister Gordon Brown kündigt eine von Sir John Chilcot geleitete Untersuchung an, 'um den Zeitraum vom Sommer 2001 bis Ende Juli 2009 zu untersuchen, der die Vorbereitung auf den Konflikt im Irak, die militärischen Aktionen und deren Folgen umfasst'. 24. November 2009: Erste öffentliche Anhörungen finden statt. 29. Januar 2010: Tony Blair sagt aus und erklärt, er bereue es nicht, Saddam gestürzt zu haben. Er wird bei seinem Abgang ausgebuht. 2. Februar 2011: Die abschließende öffentliche Anhörung findet statt. Der ehemalige Außenminister Jack Straw erklärt, dass Großbritannien nie eine Politik des Regimewechsels verfolgt habe. 16. November 2011: Die Veröffentlichung des Berichts wird nach einer Auseinandersetzung mit dem Cabinet Office über die Verwendung von Verschlusssachen, einschließlich Mr. Blairs privaten Nachrichten an Präsident Bush im Vorfeld des Krieges, auf mindestens Sommer 2012 verschoben. 16. Juli 2012: Sir John gibt bekannt, dass der Bericht nicht vor Mitte 2013 veröffentlicht wird, da noch keine Entscheidung darüber getroffen wurde, welche Dokumente freigegeben werden sollen. 7. November 2013: Sir John deutet an, dass sich die Veröffentlichung aufgrund eines Streits über 130 neue Transkripte von Gesprächen zwischen Brown, Blair und Bush auf unbestimmte Zeit verzögern könnte. 16. Mai 2014: David Cameron äußert die Hoffnung auf eine Veröffentlichung bis Ende des Jahres. 27. Mai 2014: Mr. Blair beteuert, dass er nicht für die Verzögerung verantwortlich sei, und erklärt, er wolle die Ergebnisse hören, damit er sich verteidigen könne. 29. Mai 2014: Es wird eine Vereinbarung getroffen, Auszüge aus dem Austausch zwischen Blair und Bush zu veröffentlichen – die vollständigen Texte bleiben jedoch vertraulich. 14. September 2014: Quellen in Whitehall berichten, dass Sir John weiterhin die Freigabe von Verschlusssachen von Beamten beantragt und juristische Schreiben an wichtige Labour-Politiker noch nicht versandt wurden. Es ist nun unwahrscheinlich, dass der Bericht vor den Parlamentswahlen 2015 veröffentlicht wird.

article_content: A vehicle laden with explosives detonated outside a well-known restaurant in Mogadishu, Somalia, on Sunday evening, resulting in at least 10 fatalities, according to police reports. Fifteen individuals sustained injuries in the explosion, which occurred in the heart of Mogadishu, as reported by senior Somali police officer Farhah Aden. He indicated that the death toll could potentially increase due to the severity of the injuries sustained by numerous victims. The vehicle was positioned near the entrance of the Oromo restaurant before the detonation, Aden stated. The restaurant is frequented by Somali government officials and is situated a few kilometers from the nation's parliament. An eyewitness recounted observing a plume of smoke ascending into the sky following the explosion. 'I was inside the restaurant when the explosion occurred,' said Ibrahim Mohamed. 'I heard a loud explosion originating from the building's entrance, and upon exiting, I observed deceased individuals lying on chairs where they had been sitting, using the Internet.' The Al-Shabaab terror group has claimed responsibility for the attack, as stated by the group's spokesman, Sheikh Abdiaziz Abu Musab. The group's leader was killed in an American airstrike last month. Intelligence reports at the time suggested the group was planning retaliatory attacks following the death of Ahmed Godane.

article_content: Ian Hayton, a 43-year-old father from Garston, Liverpool, was apprehended by police after they observed him using his mobile phone while driving. A subsequent search of his car revealed 20 kilograms of high-grade heroin. Hayton attempted to flee from officers after being spotted using his phone while leaving a pub. He drove through red lights and roundabouts, endangering pedestrians during a five-mile pursuit. Hayton's girlfriend was also present in the Skoda Octavia. Traffic eventually blocked Hayton on Mackets Lane, Liverpool, leading to his arrest. Officers discovered the heroin, with an estimated value of £1 million, in the boot of the vehicle. They also found a list of names and numbers believed to belong to potential customers. This incident occurred on February 16. According to Stephen McNally, the prosecuting attorney, Hayton exclaimed, 'Is it just because I was on my mobile phone?'. The search of the vehicle revealed the reason for his attempt to evade the police. Judge Miss Recorder Goddard initially sentenced Hayton to 10 years in jail. However, she reduced the sentence after considering the impact on his severely disabled 22-year-old son, who requires extensive care, according to the Liverpool Echo. Michael Bagley, Hayton's barrister, argued that Hayton's stressful personal life led to substance abuse and involvement in drug dealing. He stated that those in leading roles in drug operations typically avoid direct involvement in moving drugs. Instead, they exploit and manipulate others into their criminal organizations through dependency, debt, and pressure. Hayton admitted to dangerous driving and conspiracy to supply drugs and was also banned from driving. Detective Inspector Mark Baker, from the Matrix Serious Organised Crime team, stated that Hayton was 'consumed by his own greed and the desire to make money'.
